2014_subclasses.alchemist.description: An Alchemist is an expert in magical chemistry, combining reagents to produce mystical effects. Alchemists use their potions and elixirs to heal allies and hinder foes.
2014_subclasses.alchemist.tool-proficien: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with another type of artisan's tools of your choice.
2014_subclasses.alchemist.experimental-e: Whenever you finish a long rest, you can produce a number of experimental elixirs equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). You can use a bonus action to drink one of your elixirs or administer it to another creature. The elixir produces one of the following effects (your choice): Healing (regains 2d4 + Intelligence modifier hit points), Swiftness (speed increases by 10 feet for 1 hour), or Resilience (gain a +1 bonus to AC for 10 minutes).
Whenever you finish a long rest, you can produce a number of experimental elixirs equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).
2014_subclasses.alchemist.alchemical-sav: When you cast a spell using your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage.
Can add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.alchemist.restorative-re: You can cast the lesser restoration spell without expending a spell slot or requiring material components. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. (action).
2014_subclasses.alchemist.chemical-maste: You gain resistance to acid and poison damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
Gain resistance to acid and poison damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
2014_subclasses.armorer.description: An Armorer uses their artificer magic to empower a suit of armor, turning it into a powerful magical protection. The Armorer can transform their armor into different modes for combat or stealth.
2014_subclasses.armorer.tools-of-the-tra: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
Gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
2014_subclasses.armorer.arcane-armor.des: Your armor becomes magical. You can don or doff your armor as an action, and it can't be removed against your will. While wearing your armor, you gain the following benefits: You have a +1 bonus to AC, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with weapons, and you can use your armor as a spellcasting focus.
2014_subclasses.armorer.arcane-armor.sum: Can don or doff your armor as an action, and it can't be removed against your will. (action).
2014_subclasses.armorer.armor-model.desc: You can customize your armor for combat or stealth. When you finish a long rest, you can change your armor model. Choose one of the following: Guardian (you have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks, and when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make an additional melee attack from the armor's thunder gauntlets) or Infiltrator (you have advantage on Charisma (Stealth) checks, and your armor's lightning launcher deals an extra 1d6 lightning damage).
2014_subclasses.armorer.armor-model.summ: Choose one of the following: Guardian (you have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks, and when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make an additional melee attack.
2014_subclasses.armorer.extra-attack.des: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
2014_subclasses.armorer.extra-attack.sum: Can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).
2014_subclasses.armorer.armor-modificati: You learn 2 additional artificer infusions, and you can apply them to your armor. You can have up to 4 infusions active on your armor at a time.
Learn 2 additional artificer infusions, and you can apply them to your armor.
Your armor's power increases. While wearing your armor, you gain the following benefits based on your armor model: Guardian (when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to deal 1d6 thunder damage to that creature) or Infiltrator (when you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage).
Gain the following benefits based on your armor model: Guardian.
2014_subclasses.artillerist.description: An Artillerist specializes in harnessing the power of magic to create destructive energy. They can conjure a magical cannon that unleashes powerful blasts of elemental energy.
2014_subclasses.artillerist.tool-profici: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools.
2014_subclasses.artillerist.eldritch-can: You can use woodcarver's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a Small eldritch cannon in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. The cannon has AC 18 and hit points equal to five times your artificer level. You can have only one cannon at a time. As an action, you can command the cannon to move up to 15 feet. You can use a bonus action to activate the cannon, causing it to produce one of the following effects: Flamethrower (15-foot cone, 2d8 fire damage, Dexterity saving throw), Force Ballista (ranged spell attack, 2d8 force damage, push 5 feet), or Protector (10-foot radius, 1d8 + Intelligence modifier temporary hit points).
Can use woodcarver's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a Small eldritch cannon in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.artillerist.arcane-firea: You can use a wand, staff, or rod as a spellcasting focus. When you cast an artificer spell through this focus, you can roll a d8 and add it to one damage roll of the spell.
Can roll a d8 and add it to one damage roll of the spell. (action).
2014_subclasses.artillerist.explosive-ca: Your cannon's damage increases by 1d8. In addition, you can detonate your cannon as an action. Each creature within 20 feet of the cannon must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Each creature within 20 feet of the cannon must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save, or half.
2014_subclasses.artillerist.fortified-po: You and your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of your cannon. In addition, you can have two cannons at a time, and you can activate both with the same bonus action.
And your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of your cannon. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.description: A Battle Smith is a master of combat and magic, combining martial prowess with magical tinkering. They can create a powerful steel defender that fights alongside them.
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.tool-profic: You gain proficiency with smith's tools and heavy armor.
Gain proficiency with smith's tools and heavy armor. (permanent).
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.battle-read: You are proficient with martial weapons. When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls.
Can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls. (action).
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.steel-defen: You can use smith's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a steel defender in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. The defender has AC 15 + your proficiency bonus and hit points equal to 2 + your Intelligence modifier + five times your artificer level. It is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. In combat, the defender shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours.
Can use smith's tools and 10 gp worth of raw materials to create a steel defender in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. (action).
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.extra-attac: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.arcane-jolt: When you hit a creature with a magic weapon, you can channel a burst of arcane energy into the target. The target takes an additional 2d6 force damage, and if the target is a construct, it takes an additional 2d6 force damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
The target takes an additional 2d6 force damage, and if the target is a construct, it takes an additional 2d6 force damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.battle-smith.improved-de: Your Arcane Jolt and steel defender become more powerful. The extra damage of Arcane Jolt increases to 4d6. In addition, when your steel defender uses its Deflect Attack feature, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier.
In addition, when your steel defender uses its Deflect Attack feature, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier. (action).
2014_subclasses.ancestral-guardian.descr: Some barbarians hail from cultures that revere their ancestors. These tribes teach that the warriors of the past linger in the world as mighty spirits, who can guide and protect the living. When barbarians who follow this path rage, they channel these protective spirits, using them to guard their allies and enemies.
2014_subclasses.ancestral-guardian.ances: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, spectral warriors appear when you enter your rage. While you're raging, the first creature you hit with an attack on your turn has disadvantage on any attack target that isn't you or the warrior. Additionally, if the target tries to make an attack while within 5 feet of you, it must first make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target must choose a different target or the attack fails. On a successful save, the target can make its attack as normal. This effect lasts until the start of your next turn.
Additionally, if the target tries to make an attack while within 5 feet of you, it must first make a Wisdom saving throw. (action).
2014_subclasses.ancestral-guardian.spiri: Beginning at 6th level, the guardian spirits that aid you can provide protection to those you defend. If a creature you can see takes damage while within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. You can reduce the damage by an additional 1d6 at 10th level (3d6) and at 14th level (4d6).
Can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.ancestral-guardian.consu: At 10th level, you cast the augury or clairvoyance spell, without requiring a spell slot or material components, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a long rest. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
At 10th level, you cast the augury or clairvoyance spell, without requiring a spell slot or material components, and you regain the ability to cast it this way when you.
2014_subclasses.ancestral-guardian.venge: At 14th level, your ancestral spirits can hinder your foes even more. When you use your Spirit Shield to reduce the damage of an attack, the attacker takes an amount of force damage equal to the damage your Spirit Shield prevents.
The attacker takes an amount of force damage equal to the damage your Spirit Shield prevents. (action).
2014_subclasses.berserker.description: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end--that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker's rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.
2014_subclasses.berserker.frenzy.descrip: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).
2014_subclasses.berserker.frenzy.summary: For the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. (bonus action).
Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.
The effect is suspended for the duration of the rage. (action).
2014_subclasses.berserker.intimidating-p:
Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
 If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.
Can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours. (action).
2014_subclasses.berserker.retaliation.de: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.
2014_subclasses.berserker.retaliation.su: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against.
2014_subclasses.path-of-the-beast.descri: Barbarians who walk the Path of the Beast draw their power from a primal animal spark within their souls. When they rage, that spark manifests as a physical transformation, granting them natural weapons and bestial traits in battle.
2014_subclasses.path-of-the-beast.form-o: Manifest a natural weapon (Bite, Claws, or Tail) when entering rage.

When you enter your rage, you can transform, revealing the bestial power within you. Until the rage ends, you manifest a natural weapon. It counts as a simple melee weapon for you, and you add your Strength modifier to the attack and damage rolls when you attack with it. You choose the weapon each time you rage: Bite (1d8 piercing, heal PB hit points once per turn when below half HP), Claws (1d6 slashing, make an additional claw attack once per turn when taking the Attack action), or Tail (1d8 piercing with reach, reaction to add 1d8 to your AC against an attack that would hit you).
2014_subclasses.path-of-the-beast.bestia: Natural weapons count as magical; adapt movement with climbing, swimming, or jumping.

The feral spirit within you grows stronger, altering your physical form. The natural weapons you manifest with Form of the Beast now count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. In addition, when you finish a short or long rest, you can choose one of the following benefits until your next rest: Swimming (gain swimming speed equal to walking speed and can breathe underwater), Climbing (gain climbing speed equal to walking speed and climb difficult surfaces without checks), or Jumping (extend your jump distance by rolling an Athletics check and adding the total to the distance in feet).
2014_subclasses.path-of-the-beast.infect: Curse a creature you strike with natural weapons to deal 2d12 psychic damage or strike an ally.

When you hit a creature with your natural weapons while raging, the beast within you can curse your target with rabid fury. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier) or suffer one of the following effects (your choice): the target must use its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature of your choice that you can see, or the target takes 2d12 psychic damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses upon finishing a long rest.
2014_subclasses.path-of-the-beast.call-t: Rally your pack to gain 5 temp HP per ally and grant allies +1d6 damage on attacks.

The beast within you grows so powerful that you can spread its ferocity to your companions and be sustained by their presence. When you enter your rage, you can choose a number of willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one). You gain 5 temporary hit points for each creature that accepts this feature. Until the rage ends, the chosen creatures each gain an extra 1d6 damage on their melee weapon damage rolls once per turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses upon a long rest.
2014_subclasses.path-of-wild-magic.descr: Many places in the multiverse abound with beauty, intense emotion, and rampant magic; the Feywild and Upper Planes are among them. Barbarians influenced by these realms burst into magical chaos when their rage begins.
2014_subclasses.path-of-wild-magic.magic: Sense the presence of any spell or magic item within 60 feet.

As an action, you can open your awareness to the presence of concentrated magic. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any spell or magic item within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover. When you sense a spell, you learn its school of magic. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
2014_subclasses.path-of-wild-magic.wild-: Roll a d8 on the Wild Magic table upon raging to produce a chaotic magical surge.

Magical energy roils inside you. Whenever you enter your rage, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table to determine the magical effect produced: 1: Each creature of your choice within 30 feet takes 1d12 necrotic damage and you gain 1d12 temp HP. 2: Teleport up to 30 feet as a bonus action each turn. 3: Summon an intangible spirit within 30 feet that explodes for 1d6 force damage on hit. 4: A magic light infuses your weapon, dealing +1d6 force damage and gaining the light and thrown properties. 5: Retaliate against attackers with 1d6 force damage when struck. 6: Gain a +1 AC protective aura for yourself and allies within 10 feet. 7: The ground within 15 feet of you turns difficult terrain for enemies. 8: Shoot a beam of radiant light up to 30 feet blinding the target and dealing 1d6 radiant damage.
2014_subclasses.path-of-wild-magic.bolst: Bolster an ally to give +1d3 on attack rolls/ability checks or restore a 1st-3rd level spell slot.

You can harness your wild magic to bolster yourself or a companion. As an action, you can touch a creature (which can be yourself) and confer one of the following benefits: For 10 minutes, the creature can add a 1d3 roll to any attack roll or ability check it makes. Or, roll a 1d3 to restore one expended spell slot to the creature of a level equal to or lower than the rolled number. Once you confer either benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a use of your rage to do so.
2014_subclasses.path-of-wild-magic.unsta: Reroll your Wild Magic Surge table effect when taking damage or failing a saving throw.

When you are imperiled during your rage, the magic within you can lash out. Immediately after you take damage or fail a saving throw while raging, you can use your reaction to roll on the Wild Magic table and immediately produce the new effect, replacing your current surge effect.
2014_subclasses.path-of-wild-magic.contr: Roll twice on the Wild Magic Surge table and choose which effect manifests.

Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to produce. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the table.
2014_subclasses.storm-herald.description: All barbarians harbor a fury within. Their rage grants them superior strength, durability, and speed. Barbarians who follow the Path of the Storm Herald learn to transform that rage into a mantle of primal magic, which swirls around them. When in a fury, a barbarian of this path can protect their allies and harm their foes with the power of the elements.
Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. Your aura has a different effect depending on the environment you choose when you enter your rage: Desert, Sea, or Tundra.

Desert: When this effect is activated, all other creatures of your choice in your aura take 2 fire damage each. The damage increases to 3 at 5th level, 4 at 10th level, 5 at 15th level, and 6 at 20th level.

Sea: When this effect is activated, you can choose one other creature you can see in your aura. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. The target takes 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 2d6 at 10th level, 3d6 at 15th level, and 4d6 at 20th level.

Tundra: When this effect is activated, each creature of your choice in your aura gains 2 temporary hit points, which last until your rage ends. The temporary hit points increase to 3 at 5th level, 4 at 10th level, 5 at 15th level, and 6 at 20th level.
The target takes 1d6 lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. (action).
At 6th level, the storm grants you benefits even when your rage isn't active. You gain resistance to the damage type associated with your chosen environment: fire (Desert), lightning (Sea), or cold (Tundra).

In addition, as an action, you can create a bolt of lightning or a wave of freezing cold. If you chose Desert, you can cast the produce flame cantrip, requiring no material components. If you chose Sea, you can cast the create or destroy water spell, requiring no material components. If you chose Tundra, you can cast the fog cloud spell, requiring no material components. You can cast these spells without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast them this way when you finish a long rest.
Gain resistance to the damage type associated with your chosen environment: fire (Desert), lightning (Sea), or cold (Tundra). (action).
2014_subclasses.storm-herald.shielding-s: At 10th level, the storm you channel grows powerful enough to resist magical effects. Each creature of your choice that you can see in your aura has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Each creature of your choice that you can see in your aura has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
2014_subclasses.storm-herald.raging-stor:
At 14th level, the storm you channel responds to your fury. When you use your Storm Aura, you can choose one additional effect based on your chosen environment:

Desert: When a creature starts its turn in your aura, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn.

Sea: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to the attacker equal to your rage damage bonus.

Tundra: When a creature starts its turn in your aura, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.
On a failed save, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of its next turn. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.totem.description:
The Path of the Totem Warrior is a spiritual journey, as the barbarian accepts a spirit animal as guide, protector, and inspiration. In battle, your totem spirit fills you with supernatural might, adding magical fuel to your barbarian rage.

Most barbarian tribes consider a totem animal to be kin to the members of the tribe. It is rare for an individual to have more than one totem animal spirit in a lifetime, though exceptions exist.
2014_subclasses.totem.spirit-seeker.desc: Yours is a path that seeks attunement with the natural world, granting you a kinship with beasts. At 3rd level when you adopt this path, you gain the ability to cast the beast sense and speak with animals spells, but only as rituals.
2014_subclasses.totem.spirit-seeker.summ: Yours is a path that seeks attunement with the natural world, granting you a kinship with beasts.
2014_subclasses.totem.totem-spirit.descr: At 3rd level, when you adopt this path, you choose a totem spirit and gain a totem feature. You must make or acquire a physical totem object — an amulet or similar adornment — that incorporates fur or feathers, claws, teeth, or bones of the animal you choose. At your option, you also gain minor physical attributes from your totem animal. Your choices and the associated benefits are: Bear. While raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage. Eagle. While raging, other creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you, and you can use the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn. Wolf. While raging, your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you that is hostile to you.
2014_subclasses.totem.totem-spirit.summa: Your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you that is hostile to you. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.totem.aspect-of-the-beas: At 6th level, you gain a magical benefit based on the totem animal you choose. You can choose the same animal you chose at 3rd level or a different one. Bear. You gain the might of a bear. Your carrying capacity (including load, lift, and push) is doubled, and you have advantage on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects. Eagle. You gain the eyesight of an eagle. You can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty, able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. Additionally, dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks. Wolf. You gain the hunting sensibilities of a wolf. You can track other creatures while traveling at a brisk pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace.
Your carrying capacity (including load, lift, and push) is doubled, and you have advantage on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects. (action).
2014_subclasses.totem.spirit-walker.desc: At 10th level, you can cast the commune with nature spell, but only as a ritual. When you do so, a spiritual version of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast makes itself known to you and appears somewhere on the land you are in.
2014_subclasses.totem.spirit-walker.summ: A spiritual version of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast makes itself known to you and appears somewhere on the land you.
2014_subclasses.totem.totemic-attunement: At 14th level, you gain a magical benefit based on a totem animal you choose. You can choose the same animal you chose at 3rd level or a different one. Bear. While raging, any creature within 5 feet of you that's hostile to you has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another character with this feature. An enemy is immune to this effect if it can't see or hear you or if it can't be frightened. Eagle. While raging, you have a flying speed equal to your current speed. This benefit works only in short bursts; you fall if you end your turn in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft. Wolf. While raging, you can use a bonus action on your turn to knock a Large or smaller creature prone when you hit it with a melee weapon attack.
Any creature within 5 feet of you that's hostile to you has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another character with this feature. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.zealot.description: Some deities inspire their followers to channel unrelenting ferocity. These barbarians are zealots—warriors who channel their rage into powerful displays of divine might.
2014_subclasses.zealot.divine-fury.descr: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can channel divine power to fuel your attacks. If you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack while raging, you can roll one additional damage die and add it to the damage of the attack. The damage is of the same type as the attack's normal damage type. At 14th level, you roll two additional damage dice instead of one.
2014_subclasses.zealot.divine-fury.summa: The damage is of the same type as the attack's normal damage type. (action).
2014_subclasses.zealot.warrior-of-the-go: At 6th level, the divine power that fuels your rage allows you to shrug off fatal blows. When you would drop to 0 hit points as a result of taking damage, you can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). On a success, you drop to 1 hit point instead. After the saving throw succeeds, you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
Can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). (action).
2014_subclasses.zealot.fanatical-focus.d: At 10th level, the divine power that fuels your rage can help you push through harm. If you fail a saving throw while raging, you can reroll it, and you must use the new roll. You can use this ability only once per rage.
2014_subclasses.zealot.fanatical-focus.s: At 10th level, the divine power that fuels your rage can help you push through harm. (action).
At 14th level, you learn to channel divine power to inspire zealotry in others. As a bonus action, you unleash a battle cry infused with divine energy. Up to ten creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear you have advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Up to ten creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear you have advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next.
2014_subclasses.college-of-creation.desc: Bards of the College of Creation believe that the cosmos was drawn into existence through the Song of Creation, and that fragments of that primordial music still resound in every particle of matter.
2014_subclasses.college-of-creation.mote: Bardic Inspiration creates a dancing mote of potential granting extra effects on checks, attacks, and saves.

Whenever you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can utter a note from the Song of Creation to create a Tiny mote of potential, which orbits the creature within 5 feet. When the creature uses the die, the mote provides an additional effect: Ability Check (roll twice and pick highest), Attack Roll (explodes with thunder damage equal to inspiration roll to target and creatures within 5 ft), or Saving Throw (gain temp HP equal to the roll plus your Charisma modifier).
2014_subclasses.college-of-creation.perf: Magically create one nonmagical item worth up to 20 times your bard level in gold.

As an action, you can channel the magic of the Song of Creation to create one nonmagical item of your choice in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. The item must be of a size no larger than Medium, and its value can be no more than 20 times your bard level in gp. The item glistens faintly and lasts for a number of hours equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a 2nd-level or higher spell slot.
2014_subclasses.college-of-creation.anim: Animate a Large or smaller nonmagical object into a friendly Dancing Item construct.

As an action, you can animate one Large or smaller nonmagical item within 30 feet of you. The item uses the Dancing Item stat block, is friendly to you and your companions, and obeys your mental commands as a bonus action. It has an aura of 10 feet that increases ally movement and slows enemies. It remains animated for 1 hour, until reduced to 0 HP, or until you die. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a 3rd-level or higher spell slot.
2014_subclasses.college-of-creation.crea: Create multiple items with Performance of Creation, with no gold cost limit and up to Huge size.

When you use your Performance of Creation feature, you can now create more than one item at a time. The number of items equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of two). One of the items can be Huge, and the gp limit on the items' value no longer applies.
2014_subclasses.college-of-eloquence.des: Adherents of the College of Eloquence master the art of oratory. Persuasion is elevated to an art form, and their silver tongues can turn foes into friends and unravel the resolve of their adversaries.
2014_subclasses.college-of-eloquence.sil: Treat any roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10 for Persuasion and Deception checks.
You are a master at saying the right thing at the right time. When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
2014_subclasses.college-of-eloquence.uns: Expend a Bardic Inspiration die to subtract the roll from a target's next saving throw.

You can spin words laced with magic that unsettle a creature and cause it to doubt itself. As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Roll the Bardic Inspiration die. The creature must subtract the number rolled from the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.
2014_subclasses.college-of-eloquence.unf: A creature does not lose its Bardic Inspiration die if it fails the roll.

Your inspiring words are so persuasive that others feel driven to succeed. When a creature adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to its ability check, attack roll, or saving throw and the roll fails, the creature can keep the Bardic Inspiration die to use again on a future roll.
2014_subclasses.college-of-eloquence.uni: Make your speech completely understandable to any creatures regardless of language.

You have gained the ability to make your speech intelligible to any creature. As an action, choose one or more creatures within 60 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). The chosen creatures can magically understand you, regardless of the language you speak, for 1 hour. You can use this feature once per long rest, or by expending a spell slot.
2014_subclasses.college-of-eloquence.inf: Inspire another creature without expending a die when an ally succeeds using inspiration.

When you successfully inspire someone, the power of your eloquence can spread to someone else. When a creature within 60 feet of you adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to its roll and the roll succeeds, you can use your reaction to grant another creature within 60 feet a Bardic Inspiration die without expending any of your Bardic Inspiration uses.
2014_subclasses.glamour.description: The College of Glamour is the home of bards who mastered their craft in the vibrant realm of the Feywild or under the tutelage of someone who dwelled there. Tutored by satyrs, eladrin, and other fey creatures, these bards learn to use their magic to delight and captivate others.
2014_subclasses.glamour.mantle-of-inspir: When you join the College of Glamour at 3rd level, you gain the ability to weave a song of fey magic that imbues your allies with vigor and speed. As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to grant yourself a wondrous appearance. When you do so, choose up to five creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you. Each target gains 5 temporary hit points and can use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
Gain the ability to weave a song of fey magic that imbues your allies with vigor and speed. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.glamour.enthralling-perf: Starting at 6th level, you can use musical or oratorial performance to weave a song of fey magic that charms your listeners. If you perform for at least 1 minute, you can then choose a number of humanoids within 60 feet of you who watched or listened to your performance, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you. While charmed, the target idolates you and hinders anyone attempting to harm you, but it will not obey your orders. This effect ends on a target after 1 hour, if it takes damage, if you attack it, or if it witnesses you attacking its allies. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you. (action).
2014_subclasses.glamour.mantle-of-majest: At 14th level, you gain the ability to cloak yourself in a fey majesty. As a bonus action, you cast command, requiring no spell slot or material components, and you take on an appearance of unearthly beauty (as the alter self spell, but only affecting your appearance). The spell lasts for 1 minute. During that time, you can cast command as a bonus action on each of your turns, without expending a spell slot. Any creature charmed by you automatically fails its saving throw against the command spell you cast with this feature. Once you use this bonus action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to use it again.
Any creature charmed by you automatically fails its saving throw against the command spell you cast with this feature. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.college-of-spirits.descr: Bards of the College of Spirits seek to tell the stories of those who have passed on, using their magic to channel the spirits of the dead. These bards are often found in graveyards, haunted houses, and other places where the dead linger.
2014_subclasses.college-of-spirits.spiri: You employ tools that aid you in channeling spirits, such as a candle, crystal, or totem. When you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points while holding your spiritual focus, you can roll a d6 and add it to the roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
When you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores Hit Points while holding your spiritual focus, roll a d6 and add it to the damage or healing roll.
2014_subclasses.college-of-spirits.tales: You can reach out to the spirits of the dead to tell you stories. As a bonus action, you can roll a d6 and add it to your next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Can roll a d6 and add it to your next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.college-of-spirits.spiri: Your spiritual focus becomes more powerful. When you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points while holding your spiritual focus, you can roll a d8 instead of a d6 and add it to the roll.
Can roll a d8 instead of a d6 and add it to the roll. (action).
You can cast the speak with dead spell at will, without expending a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, you can ask the corpse up to seven questions, rather than five.
Can cast the speak with dead spell at will, without expending a spell slot. (action).
2014_subclasses.college-of-spirits.mysti: You can use your Tales from Beyond feature without expending a use of it. When you do so, you roll a d8 instead of a d6.
Use Tales from Beyond without expending a use. When you do so, roll a d8 instead of a d6.
2014_subclasses.swords.description: Bards of the College of Swords are called blades, and they entertain through daring feats of weapon prowess. They perform stunts such as sword swallowing, knife throwing, and juggling. Though they use their weapons to entertain, they are highly trained and skilled warriors.
2014_subclasses.swords.bonus-proficienci: When you join the College of Swords at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, scimitars, and the performer's kit.
Gain proficiency with medium armor, scimitars, and the performer's kit.
2014_subclasses.swords.fighting-style.de: At 3rd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options: Dueling, Two-Weapon Fighting, or Great Weapon Fighting. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you get to choose again.
2014_subclasses.swords.fighting-style.du: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
2014_subclasses.swords.fighting-style.tw: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.
2014_subclasses.swords.fighting-style.gr: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.
2014_subclasses.swords.fighting-style.su: Can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you get to choose again. (permanent).
2014_subclasses.swords.blade-flourish.de: At 3rd level, you learn to perform impressive displays of martial prowess and speed. Whenever you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to use one of the following flourishes: Defensive Flourish, Slashing Flourish, or Mobile Flourish. Defensive Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to add the number you roll to your AC until the start of your next turn. Slashing Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal extra damage to the target you hit and to any other creature of your choice within 5 feet of you. Mobile Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to push the target you hit up to 15 feet away from you, plus a number of feet equal to the number you roll on the Bardic Inspiration die. The target is pushed to an unoccupied space of your choice.
2014_subclasses.swords.blade-flourish.su: Slashing Flourish: You can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal extra damage to the target you hit and to any other creature of your choice within 5.
2014_subclasses.swords.extra-attack.desc: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
2014_subclasses.swords.extra-attack.summ: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).
2014_subclasses.swords.master-flourish.d: Starting at 14th level, whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.
2014_subclasses.swords.master-flourish.s: Starting at 14th level, whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die. (action).
2014_subclasses.whispers.description: Most bards share their tales with a wide audience. The bards of the College of Whispers, however, use their knowledge to uncover secrets and turn them against others through dread and fear.
When you join the College of Whispers at 3rd level, you learn to make your weapon attacks especially deadly. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage to that target. The damage increases to 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 10th level, 8d6 at 15th level, and 10d6 at 20th level.
Can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage to that target. (action).
2014_subclasses.whispers.words-of-terror: At 6th level, you can weave words of dread to frighten a creature. If you speak to a humanoid alone for at least 1 minute, you can then attempt to seed paranoia in its mind. At the end of the conversation, the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you or another creature of your choice. The frightened condition lasts for 1 hour, until the target is attacked or damaged, or until the target witnesses its allies being attacked or damaged. If the target succeeds on the saving throw, the target doesn't suspect that you tried to frighten it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
At the end of the conversation, the target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. (action).
2014_subclasses.whispers.mantle-of-whisp: At 14th level, you gain the ability to adopt a humanoid's persona. When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can magically capture its shadow using your reaction. You retain this shadow until you use it or finish a long rest. You can use the shadow as a disguise, as the disguise self spell, but it affects only your appearance. You can also use the shadow to gain information about the creature, as the speak with dead spell, but you can only ask one question. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Can magically capture its shadow using your reaction. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.lore.description: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as diverse as scholarly tomes and peasant tales. Whether singing folk ballads in taverns or elaborate compositions in royal courts, these bards use their gifts to hold audiences spellbound. When the applause dies down, the audience members might find themselves questioning everything they held to be true, from their faith in the priesthood of the local temple to their loyalty to the king. The loyalty of these bards lies in the pursuit of beauty and truth, not in fealty to a monarch or following the tenets of a deity. A noble who keeps such a bard as a herald or advisor knows that the bard would rather be honest than politic. The college's members gather in libraries and sometimes in actual colleges, complete with classrooms and dormitories, to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.
2014_subclasses.lore.bonus-proficiencies: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
Gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
2014_subclasses.lore.cutting-words.descr:
Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.
When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.
You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.
2014_subclasses.lore.cutting-words.summa: When a creature within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, use your reaction to expend one Bardic Inspiration use and subtract the Bardic Inspiration die roll from the creature's roll. Must be used before the GM determines the outcome.
2014_subclasses.lore.additional-magical-: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.
Choose one spell from any class
Choose another spell from any class
The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know. (action).
2014_subclasses.lore.peerless-skill.desc: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.
2014_subclasses.lore.peerless-skill.summ: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. (action).
2014_subclasses.valor.description:
Bards of the College of Valor are daring skalds, telling tales of great heroes and performing deeds worthy of song. They wander the land to witness great events firsthand and see the deeds of legendary heroes.

As they travel from place to place, these bards inspire others with songs and stories of past glories, stirring their audiences to greatness and spurring them to action. The college's members gather to share their lore with one another and celebrate their common bond.
2014_subclasses.valor.bonus-proficiencie: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
Gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
2014_subclasses.valor.combat-inspiration: Also at 3rd level, you learn to inspire others in combat. A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack, after seeing the roll but before knowing whether it hits or misses.
Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against.
2014_subclasses.valor.extra-attack.descr: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
2014_subclasses.valor.extra-attack.summa: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).
2014_subclasses.valor.battle-magic.descr: At 14th level, you have mastered the art of weaving spellcasting and weapon use together. When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
2014_subclasses.valor.battle-magic.summa: Can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.arcana.description: Magic is an energy that suffuses the multiverse. Clerics of the Arcana Domain revere the deities of magic, knowing that arcane magic and divine devotion can weave together in sublime mystery.
2014_subclasses.arcana.arcane-initiate.s: Gain proficiency in Arcana and learn two wizard cantrips that count as cleric cantrips.
2014_subclasses.arcana.arcane-initiate.d: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Arcana skill, and you gain two cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. For you, these cantrips count as cleric cantrips.
2014_subclasses.arcana.arcana-domain-spe: Gain domain spells at levels 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.
1st: Detect Magic, Magic Missile; 3rd: Magic Weapon, Nondetection; 5th: Dispel Magic, Magic Circle; 7th: Arcane Eye, Leomund's Secret Chest; 9th: Planar Binding, Teleportation Circle.
2014_subclasses.arcana.channel-divinity-: Turn or banish celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend creatures within 30 feet.

As an action, you present your holy symbol and one celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom save or be turned for 1 minute. Starting at 5th level, turned creatures of low CR are banished to their home plane instead.
2014_subclasses.arcana.spell-breaker.sum: When you heal an ally with a spell, end one spell of equal or lower level on that ally.
2014_subclasses.arcana.spell-breaker.des: Starting at 6th level, when you restore hit points to an ally with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also end one spell of your choice on that creature. The level of the spell you end must be equal to or lower than the level of the spell slot you used to cast the healing spell.
2014_subclasses.arcana.potent-spellcasti: Add Wisdom modifier to cleric cantrip damage.
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.
2014_subclasses.arcana.arcane-mastery.su: Learn four wizard spells (one each of 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th level) as domain spells.
2014_subclasses.arcana.arcane-mastery.de: At 17th level, you choose four spells from the wizard spell list, one from each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th. You add them to your domain spells, always prepared and casting them as cleric spells.
2014_subclasses.death.description: The Death domain is concerned with the forces that cause death, as well as the negative energy that powers undead creatures. Clerics of death are feared necromancers and heralds of finality.
At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.
2014_subclasses.death.reaper.summary: Target two adjacent creatures with necromancy cantrips that normally target one.
2014_subclasses.death.reaper.description: At 1st level, when the cleric casts a necromancy cantrip that normally targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.
2014_subclasses.death.death-domain-spell: Gain domain spells at levels 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.
1st: False Life, Ray of Sickness; 3rd: Blindness/Deafness, Ray of Enfeeblement; 5th: Animate Dead, Vampiric Touch; 7th: Blight, Death Ward; 9th: Antilife Shell, Cloudkill.
2014_subclasses.death.channel-divinity-t: Add 5 + (2 x cleric level) necrotic damage to a successful melee attack.
Starting at 2nd level, when the cleric hits a creature with a melee attack, the cleric can use Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage to the target equal to 5 + twice his or her cleric level.
2014_subclasses.death.inescapable-destru: Necrotic damage dealt by your cleric spells and Channel Divinity ignores resistance to necrotic damage.

Starting at 6th level, the cleric's ability to channel negative energy becomes more potent. Necrotic damage dealt by the character's cleric spells and Channel Divinity options ignores resistance to necrotic damage.
2014_subclasses.death.divine-strike.summ: Once on each turn, deal extra 1d8 necrotic damage on a weapon hit (2d8 at 14th).
2014_subclasses.death.divine-strike.desc: At 8th level, the cleric gains the ability to infuse his or her weapon strikes with necrotic energy. Once on each of the cleric's turns when he or she hits a creature with a weapon attack, the cleric can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. At 14th level, this increases to 2d8.
2014_subclasses.death.improved-reaper.su: Target two adjacent creatures with 1st through 5th level necromancy spells.
2014_subclasses.death.improved-reaper.de: Starting at 17th level, when the cleric casts a necromancy spell of 1st through 5th level that targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.
2014_subclasses.forge.description: The gods of the forge are patrons of artisans who work with metal, from a humble blacksmith to an elven smith who mithral. The gods of the forge teach that, with patience and hard work, even the most intractable metal can be transformed from a lump of iron into a beautiful object. Clerics of the forge domain are the divine embodiment of the power of the forge.
When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
Gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools. (action).
2014_subclasses.forge.blessing-of-the-fo: At 1st level, you gain the ability to imbue magic into a weapon or armor. At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC (armor) or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls (weapon). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Gain the ability to imbue magic into a weapon or armor.
2014_subclasses.forge.channel-divinity-a: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to create a nonmagical item that is worth no more than 100 gp. The item must be made of metal, and you must spend 10 minutes in prayer and work to create it. The item can be a suit of armor, a weapon, a set of tools, or another object. The object appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. If you create a weapon, it is a simple or martial weapon of your choice. If you create a suit of armor, it is light, medium, or heavy armor of your choice. If you create a set of tools, they are artisan's tools of your choice.
The item must be made of metal, and you must spend 10 minutes in prayer and work to create it. (action).
Starting at 6th level, your mastery of the forge grants you special resistances. You gain resistance to fire damage. In addition, while you are wearing heavy armor, you have a +1 bonus to AC.
Gain resistance to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, gain a +1 bonus to AC.
2014_subclasses.forge.divine-strike.desc: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
2014_subclasses.forge.divine-strike.summ: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.forge.saint-of-forge-and: At 17th level, your blessed affinity with the forge gains divine benefits. You gain immunity to fire damage. In addition, while you are wearing heavy armor, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.
Gain immunity to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.
2014_subclasses.grave.description: Gods of the grave watch over the line between life and death. To these deities, death and the afterlife are a foundational part of the multiverse. To desecrate the peace of the dead is an abomination. Deities of the grave include Kelemvor, Wee Jas, and the ancestors of many cultures.
When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.
2014_subclasses.grave.circle-of-mortalit: At 1st level, you gain the ability to manipulate the line between life and death. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. In addition, you learn the spare the dying cantrip, which doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. For you, it has a range of 30 feet, and you can cast it as a bonus action.
Instead use the highest number possible for each die. (bonus action).
At 1st level, you gain the ability to sense the presence of the undead. As an action, you can open your awareness to magically detect undead. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from divination magic. This sense doesn't tell you anything about the creature's capabilities or identity. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from divination.
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to mark a creature close to death for destruction. As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, cursing it until the end of your next turn. The next time you or an ally of yours hits the cursed creature with an attack, the creature has vulnerability to all damage from that attack, and then the curse ends.
Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, cursing it until the end of your next turn. (action).
2014_subclasses.grave.sentinel-at-death-: At 6th level, you gain the ability to impede death's progress. When you or a creature within 30 feet of you succeeds on a death saving throw or succeeds on a saving throw against a disease or effect that causes the poisoned condition, you can use your reaction to cancel the effect. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Can use your reaction to cancel the effect. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.grave.divine-strike.desc: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra extra damage increases to 2d8.
2014_subclasses.grave.divine-strike.summ: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.grave.keeper-of-souls.de: Starting at 17th level, you can seize a trace of vitality from a soul that has recently passed on. When a creature you can see dies within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a Charisma check (DC 10). On a success, you steal some of the creature's life force, and you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. That creature gains temporary hit points equal to the result of the check. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
2014_subclasses.grave.keeper-of-souls.su: Can use your reaction to make a Charisma check (DC 10). (reaction).
2014_subclasses.knowledge.description:
The Knowledge domain represents the pursuit of knowledge and understanding of the world and the gods. Its clerics are scholars, sages, and seekers of truth, using their divine gifts to uncover secrets and illuminate the mysteries of existence.

Gods of knowledge—including Oghma, Boccob, Gilean, and Aureon—value learning and understanding above all. Some teach that knowledge is to be gathered and shared in libraries and universities, while others believe it should be kept secret and used only by the worthy.
2014_subclasses.knowledge.blessings-of-k: At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice and gain two skills of your choice.
At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice and gain two skills of your choice.
2014_subclasses.knowledge.channel-divini: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to tap into a reservoir of knowledge. As an action, you become proficient in one skill or tool of your choice until you finish a short or long rest. You can use this feature again after a short or long rest.
Can use this feature again after a short or long rest. (action).
At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to command it, probe it, or probe its memories.
At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. (action).
2014_subclasses.knowledge.potent-spellca: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells. (action).
2014_subclasses.knowledge.visions-of-the: Starting at 17th level, you can call upon your deity to reveal visions of the past. You can receive visions of the past by spending at least 1 minute in meditation and prayer, and you can receive visions of the past of a specific object, creature, or location.
Starting at 17th level, you can call upon your deity to reveal visions of the past. (action).
2014_subclasses.life.description: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy--one of the fundamental forces of the universe--that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality and health through healing the sick and wounded, caring for those in need, and driving away the forces of death and undeath. Almost any non-evil deity can claim influence over this domain, particularly agricultural deities, sun gods, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community.
2014_subclasses.life.bonus-proficiency.d: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.
2014_subclasses.life.disciple-of-life.de: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.
2014_subclasses.life.disciple-of-life.su: Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's.
2014_subclasses.life.channel-divinity-pr:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.
As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level.
Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.
Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. (action).
2014_subclasses.life.blessed-healer.desc: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.
2014_subclasses.life.blessed-healer.summ: Regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.
2014_subclasses.life.divine-strike.descr: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
2014_subclasses.life.divine-strike.summa: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage.
2014_subclasses.life.supreme-healing.des: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.
2014_subclasses.life.supreme-healing.sum: Instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12. (action).
2014_subclasses.light.description:
The Light domain represents the power of light, fire, and revelation. Its clerics are beacons of hope and clarity, using radiant energy to burn away darkness, undeath, and deception.

Gods of light—including Lathander, Pelor, Ra, and Apollo—promote the ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty, often using the symbol of the sun. Gods of the Light domain are often associated with fire as a symbol of purity and truth.
2014_subclasses.light.bonus-cantrip.desc: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.
2014_subclasses.light.bonus-cantrip.summ: Learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice. (action).
2014_subclasses.light.warding-flare.desc: At 1st level, you can interpose divine light between yourself and an enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker. An attacker can't benefit from this feature if it can't see or is immune to being blinded. You can use this number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
2014_subclasses.light.warding-flare.summ: Can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.light.channel-divinity-r: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to flood an area with radiant energy.
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to flood an area with radiant energy. (action).
2014_subclasses.light.improved-flare.des: Starting at 6th level, you can cast the fireball spell once per long rest.
2014_subclasses.light.improved-flare.sum: Starting at 6th level, you can cast the fireball spell once per long rest.
2014_subclasses.light.potent-spellcastin: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells. (action).
2014_subclasses.light.corona-of-light.de: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to emanate a bright light. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that. Creatures of your choice in the bright light have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and on saving throws against spells that deal fire or radiant damage. You can end this effect on yourself early by using a bonus action to dismiss it.
2014_subclasses.light.corona-of-light.su: Creatures of your choice in the bright light have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and on saving throws against spells that deal fire or radiant damage. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.nature.description:
The Nature domain represents the power of the natural world. Its clerics are guardians of the wild, calling upon the primal forces of nature to protect the land and all its creatures.

Gods of nature—including Silvanus, Mielikki, and the Oak Father—revere the natural world and protect it from those who would do it harm. They teach that all living things are connected and that the balance of nature must be maintained.
2014_subclasses.nature.acolyte-of-nature: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice.
At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice.
2014_subclasses.nature.charm-animals-and: Starting at 1st level, you can use your action to charm one beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until you or your allies damage it.
Starting at 1st level, you can use your action to charm one beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. (action).
2014_subclasses.nature.channel-divinity-: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to charm animals and plants. As an action, you touch a beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until you or your allies damage it.
Touch a beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. (action).
2014_subclasses.nature.dampen-elements.d: Starting at 6th level, you can use your reaction to reduce damage. When you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of damage.
2014_subclasses.nature.dampen-elements.s: Cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of damage. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.nature.potent-spellcasti: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells. (action).
Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to charm beasts and plants. When you use your Channel Divinity to charm animals and plants, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 10 minutes or until you or your allies damage it.
The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 10 minutes or until you or your allies damage it. (action).
2014_subclasses.order.description: The Order Domain represents devotion to discipline, law, and structure. Clerics of Order strive to establish stability, harmony, and righteous command over chaos and wickedness.
2014_subclasses.order.bonus-proficiencie: Gain proficiency with heavy armor and your choice of Intimidation or Persuasion.
You gain proficiency with heavy armor. You also gain proficiency in the Intimidation or Persuasion skill (your choice).
2014_subclasses.order.voice-of-authority: When you cast a 1st-level or higher spell targeting an ally, that ally can make a weapon attack as a reaction.

You can invoke the power of law to drive an ally to strike. Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that targets an ally, you can direct that ally to use its reaction immediately after the spell to make one weapon attack against a creature of your choice that you can see. If the spell targets more than one ally, you choose the ally who can make the attack.
2014_subclasses.order.order-domain-spell: Gain domain spells at levels 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.

You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Order Domain Spells table: 1st: Command, Heroism; 3rd: Hold Person, Zone of Truth; 5th: Mass Healing Word, Slow; 7th: Compulsion, Locate Creature; 9th: Commune, Dominate Person.
2014_subclasses.order.channel-divinity-o: Charm creatures within 30 feet and force them to immediately drop weapons they are holding.

As an action, you present your holy symbol, and each creature of your choice that can see or hear you within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn or until it takes damage. You can also cause any of the charmed creatures to drop what they are holding when they fail the saving throw.
2014_subclasses.order.embodiment-of-the-: Cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher with a casting time of 1 action as a bonus action.

You have become remarkably adept at channeling order. If you cast a spell of the enchantment school using a spell slot of 1st level or higher, you can change the spell's casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting, provided the spell's normal casting time is 1 action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier per long rest.
2014_subclasses.order.divine-strike.summ: Once on each of your turns, deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage on a weapon hit (2d8 at 14th).
2014_subclasses.order.divine-strike.desc: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
2014_subclasses.order.order-s-wrath.summ: Enemies you strike with Divine Strike take an extra 2d8 psychic damage the next time an ally hits them.
2014_subclasses.order.order-s-wrath.desc: Starting at 17th level, enemies you strike are cursed by your divine authority. When you deal your Divine Strike damage to a creature, you curse that creature until the start of your next turn. The next time one of your allies hits the cursed creature with an attack, the target takes an extra 2d8 psychic damage, and the curse ends.
2014_subclasses.peace.description: The balm of peace thrives at the heart of healthy communities. Clerics of the Peace Domain act as peacemakers, forging bonds between individuals and healing physical and emotional wounds.
2014_subclasses.peace.implement-of-peace: Gain proficiency in Insight, Performance, or Persuasion.
You gain proficiency in the Insight, Performance, or Persuasion skill (your choice).
2014_subclasses.peace.emboldening-bond.s: Forge a magical bond between allies, adding 1d4 to one attack, check, or saving throw each turn.
2014_subclasses.peace.emboldening-bond.d: You can forge an empowering bond between allies. As an action, you choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you (which can include yourself) equal to your proficiency bonus. For 10 minutes, while any bonded creature is within 30 feet of another, the creature can roll a 1d4 and add the number rolled to an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes once per turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
2014_subclasses.peace.peace-domain-spell: Gain domain spells at levels 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.

You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the Peace Domain Spells table: 1st: Heroism, Sanctuary; 3rd: Aid, Warding Bond; 5th: Beacon of Hope, Sending; 7th: Aura of Purity, Otiluke's Resilient Sphere; 9th: Greater Restoration, Rary's Telepathic Bond.
2014_subclasses.peace.channel-divinity-b: Move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks and heal passed creatures 2d6 + Wis.

As an action, you can use your Channel Divinity to move up to your walking speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. When you move within 5 feet of any other creature during this action, you can restore 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier hit points to that creature. A creature can receive this healing only once whenever you take this action.
2014_subclasses.peace.protective-bond.su: Bonded creatures within 30 feet can teleport to take damage in place of one another.
2014_subclasses.peace.protective-bond.de: The bond you forge between people helps them protect each other. When a creature affected by your Emboldening Bond feature is about to take damage, a second bonded creature within 30 feet of the first can use its reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the first creature. The second creature then takes all the damage instead.
2014_subclasses.peace.potent-spellcastin: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.
Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.
2014_subclasses.peace.expansive-bond.sum: Protective Bond range increases to 60 feet, and the teleporting creature gains resistance to the damage.
2014_subclasses.peace.expansive-bond.des: The benefits of your Emboldening Bond and Protective Bond features now apply when the creatures are within 60 feet of each other. Moreover, when a creature uses Protective Bond to take someone else's damage, that creature gains resistance to that damage.
2014_subclasses.tempest.description:
