You can use your action to briefly control elemental forces nearby: create harmless sensory effects like showers of sparks, puff of wind, or mist; light or snuff a candle or campfire; chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving material; or shape earth, fire, water, or mist into crude shapes for 1 minute.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.fangs-of-t: Spend 1 ki to extend unarmed strike reach by 10 ft and deal fire damage; spend extra ki for +1d10 fire.

When you use the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to cause tendrils of flame to stretch out from your fists and feet. Your reach with your unarmed strikes increases by 10 feet for that action, as well as the rest of the turn. A hit with such an attack deals fire damage instead of bludgeoning damage, and if you spend 1 additional ki point when the attack hits, it deals an extra 1d10 fire damage.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.water-whip: Spend 2 ki to create a water whip dealing 3d10 bludgeoning and pulling the target 25 ft or knocking prone.

You can spend 2 ki points as an action to create a whip of water that shoves and pulls a creature to unbalance it. A creature that you can see that is within 30 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage plus an extra 1d10 for each additional ki point spent, and you can either knock it prone or pull it up to 25 feet closer to you.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.fist-of-fo: Spend 2 ki points to cast Thunderwave.
You can spend 2 ki points to cast Thunderwave.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.sweeping-c: Spend 2 ki points to cast Burning Hands.
You can spend 2 ki points to cast Burning Hands.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.gong-of-th: Spend 3 ki points to cast Shatter.
You can spend 3 ki points to cast Shatter.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.flames-of-: Spend 4 ki points to cast Fireball.
You can spend 4 ki points to cast Fireball.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.ride-the-w: Spend 4 ki points to cast Fly on yourself.
You can spend 4 ki points to cast Fly, targeting yourself.
2014_subclasses.four-elements.river-of-h: Spend 5 ki points to cast Wall of Fire.
You can spend 5 ki points to cast Wall of Fire.
2014_subclasses.kensei.description: Monks of the Way of the Kensei train relentlessly with their weapons, to the point where they become extensions of their body. Founded on a mastery of sword fighting, the tradition has expanded to include many different weapons.
2014_subclasses.kensei.path-of-the-kense: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies. You also choose two types of Kensei Weapons: melee weapons or ranged weapons. You can change your choices each time you gain a level. You can use your choice of any Kensei Weapon as a monk weapon, and when you do so, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your Kensei Weapons.
Choose two types of melee weapons to be your kensei weapons. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with these weapons.
Choose one ranged weapon to be your kensei weapon. You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls with this weapon.
Gain proficiency with martial weapons and calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies. (action).
2014_subclasses.kensei.one-with-the-blad: At 6th level, you extend your ki into your kensei weapons. When you hit a creature with a kensei weapon, you can spend 1 ki point to do one of the following: add your Wisdom modifier to the damage of the attack, or the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you.
Can spend 1 ki point to do one of the following: add your Wisdom modifier to the damage of the attack, or the target must succeed on a Strength saving.
2014_subclasses.kensei.sharpen-the-blade: At 11th level, you gain the ability to augment your weapons with your ki. As a bonus action, you can spend up to 3 ki points to grant a kensei weapon you touch a bonus to attack and damage rolls when you attack with it. The bonus equals the number of ki points you spent. The bonus lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again. This feature has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls.
Has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.kensei.unerring-accuracy: Starting at 17th level, your mastery of the blade ensures that your strikes land. If you miss with an attack roll using a monk weapon on your turn, you can reroll the attack roll, and you must use the new roll. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.
Can reroll the attack roll, and you must use the new roll. (action).
2014_subclasses.way-of-the-long-death.de: Monks of the Way of the Long Death obsess over the meaning and mechanics of dying. They study creatures as they die and record the exact moment when the soul leaves the body.
2014_subclasses.way-of-the-long-death.to: Gain temporary hit points equal to Wisdom modifier + monk level when reducing a creature within 5 ft to 0 HP.

Your study of death allows you to extract vitality from dying creatures. When you reduce a creature within 5 feet of you to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier + your monk level (minimum 1).
2014_subclasses.way-of-the-long-death.ho: Frighten all creatures within 30 feet that can see you on a failed Wisdom saving throw.

As an action, you unleash the macabre presence of death. Each creature within 30 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
2014_subclasses.way-of-the-long-death.ma: Spend 1 ki point when reduced to 0 hit points to drop to 1 hit point instead.
Beginning at 11th level, you use your familiarity with death to escape its grasp. When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can expend 1 ki point (no action required) to have 1 hit point instead.
2014_subclasses.way-of-the-long-death.to: Spend 1 to 10 ki points on a touched creature to deal 2d10 necrotic damage per ki point spent.

Your touch channels the pure energy of death. As an action, you touch one creature within 5 feet of you and expend 1 to 10 ki points. The target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d10 necrotic damage per ki point spent on a failure, or half as much on a success.
2014_subclasses.sun-soul.description: Monks of the Way of the Sun Soul learn to channel the power of the sun into devastating attacks. They teach that the soul is a spark of the sun's divine light, and that by channeling that light, they can overcome any darkness.
2014_subclasses.sun-soul.radiant-sun-bol: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can hurl searing bolts of magical radiance. You gain a ranged spell attack that you can make as a bonus action. The attack has a range of 30 feet and uses your Dexterity modifier for the attack roll. On a hit, the target takes radiant damage equal to your Martial Arts die. You can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
The attack has a range of 30 feet and uses your Dexterity modifier for the attack roll. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.sun-soul.searing-arc-str: At 6th level, you gain the ability to channel your ki into a blast of radiant energy. Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the burning hands spell at 3rd level (save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier). You can spend additional ki points to cast the spell at a higher level. Each additional ki point you spend increases the spell's level by 1. The maximum number of extra ki points you can spend is 3.
At 6th level, you gain the ability to channel your ki into a blast of radiant energy. (action).
2014_subclasses.sun-soul.searing-sunburs: At 11th level, you gain the ability to create a ball of light that erupts in a devastating radiant explosion. As an action, you can create a sphere centered on a point you can see within 150 feet of you. The sphere has a radius of 20 feet. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 2d6 radiant damage per ki point you spend on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save is also blinded until the end of your next turn.
A creature takes 2d6 radiant damage per ki point you spend on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. (action).
2014_subclasses.sun-soul.sun-shield.desc: At 17th level, you become wreathed in a luminous, magical aura. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. You can suppress or restore this light as a bonus action. If a creature hits you with a melee attack while this light shines, you can use your reaction to deal 5 radiant damage to the creature.
2014_subclasses.sun-soul.sun-shield.summ: Shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.ancients.description:
The Oath of the Ancients is as old as the race of elves and the rituals of the druids. Sometimes called fey knights, green knights, or horned knights, paladins who swear this oath cast their lot with the side of the light in the cosmic struggle against darkness.

These paladins love the beautiful and life-giving things of the world, not necessarily because they believe in principles of honor, courage, and justice. They adorn their armor and clothing with images of growing things—leaves, antlers, or flowers—to reflect their commitment to preserving life and light in the world.
2014_subclasses.ancients.oath-spells.des:
Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.
2014_subclasses.ancients.oath-spells.sum: Gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description.
2014_subclasses.ancients.channel-divinit: You can use your Channel Divinity to invoke primeval forces to ensnare a foe. As an action, you can cause spectral vines to spring up and reach for a creature within 10 feet of you that you can see. The creature must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice) or be restrained. While restrained by the vines, the creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success, it frees itself and the vines vanish.
Can cause spectral vines to spring up and reach for a creature within 10 feet of you that you can see. (action).

You can use your Channel Divinity to utter ancient words that are painful for fey and fiends to hear. As an action, you present your holy symbol, and each fey or fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage. A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action. If the creature's true form is concealed by an illusion, shapeshifting, or other effect, that form is revealed while it is turned.
Present your holy symbol, and each fey or fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.ancients.aura-of-warding: Beginning at 7th level, ancient magic lies so heavily upon you that it forms an eldritch ward. You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to damage from spells. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
And friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to damage from spells.
2014_subclasses.ancients.undying-sentine: Starting at 15th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points and are not killed outright, you can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. Additionally, you suffer none of the drawbacks of old age, and you can't be aged magically.
Starting at 15th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points and are not killed outright, you can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. (action).
At 20th level, you can assume the form of an ancient force of nature, taking on an appearance you choose. For example, your skin might turn green or take on a bark-like texture, your hair might become leafy or moss-like, or you might sprout antlers or a lion-like mane. Using your action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits: At the start of each of your turns, you regain 10 hit points. Whenever you cast a paladin spell that has a casting time of 1 action, you can cast it using a bonus action instead. Enemy creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on saving throws against your paladin spells and Channel Divinity options. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Enemy creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on saving throws against your paladin spells and Channel Divinity options. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.devotion.description: The Oath of Devotion binds a paladin to the loftiest ideals of justice, virtue, and order. Sometimes called cavaliers, white knights, or holy warriors, these paladins meet the ideal of the knight in shining armor, acting with honor in pursuit of justice and the greater good. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some, for better or worse, hold the rest of the world to the same standards. Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods' tenets as the measure of their devotion. They hold angels--the perfect servants of good--as their ideals, and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.
2014_subclasses.devotion.oath-spells.des:
Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.
2014_subclasses.devotion.oath-spells.sum: Gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description.
2014_subclasses.devotion.channel-divinit:
As an action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with positive energy, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). The weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. If the weapon is not already magical, it becomes magical for the duration.
You can end this effect on your turn as part of any other action. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall unconscious, this effect ends.
The weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. (action).

As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead, using your Channel Divinity. Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.
A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.devotion.aura-of-devotio:
Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.
2014_subclasses.devotion.purity-of-spiri: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.
Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.
2014_subclasses.devotion.holy-nimbus.des:
At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead.
2014_subclasses.devotion.holy-nimbus.sum: Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.draconic-disciple.descri: The Oath of the Draconic Disciple binds a paladin to the ideals of dragonkind. These paladins draw power from their draconic heritage, channeling the might of dragons through their divine oath. They seek to embody the virtues of dragonkind: strength, wisdom, and majesty.
2014_subclasses.draconic-disciple.channe: As an action, you can channel the power of dragonkind to demoralize your foes. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature is frightened of you for 1 minute. A frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. (action).

As a bonus action, you can channel the power of dragonkind to augment your strength. For 1 minute, you have advantage on Strength checks, and when you deal damage with a melee weapon, you can add your Charisma modifier to the damage roll.
Have advantage on Strength checks, and when you deal damage with a melee weapon, you can add your Charisma modifier to the damage roll. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.draconic-disciple.aura-o: You emanate an aura of draconic power. Whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you makes a saving throw, that creature gains a bonus to the roll equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus.
You emanate an aura of draconic power.
2014_subclasses.draconic-disciple.dracon: The power of dragonkind flows through you. You gain resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.
Gain resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.
2014_subclasses.draconic-disciple.dragon: As an action, you can channel the full power of dragonkind, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute: You have a flying speed equal to your walking speed. You have resistance to all damage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
As an action, channel draconic power for 1 minute: gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed, resistance to all damage, and your breath weapon deals max damage.
2014_subclasses.conquest.description: The Oath of Conquest calls to paladins who seek glory in battle and the subjugation of their enemies. These paladins are the masters of combat, and they believe that victory is the ultimate expression of their faith.
2014_subclasses.conquest.channel-divinit:
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following Channel Divinity options:

Conquering Presence: As an action, you force each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. If a creature fails its save, it is frightened of you for 1 minute. The frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a successful save.

Guided Strike: When you make an attack roll, you can use your Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to the attack roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack hits or misses.
Gain the following Channel Divinity options: Conquering Presence: As an action, you force each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you to make.
2014_subclasses.conquest.aura-of-conques: Starting at 7th level, you constantly emanate a menacing aura while you are not incapacitated. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. If a creature is frightened of you, its speed is reduced to 0 while in the aura, and that creature takes psychic damage equal to half your paladin level if it ends its turn there. At 18th level, the aura extends to 30 feet.
Its speed is reduced to 0 while in the aura, and that creature takes psychic damage equal to half your paladin level if it ends its turn there.
2014_subclasses.conquest.scared-earth.de: Starting at 15th level, you can call on the power of your oath to strike fear into your foes. As an action, you can cause the ground in a 30-foot radius around you to become difficult terrain for 1 minute. In addition, the first time each turn that a creature moves into the area or starts its turn there, it takes 3d6 psychic damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
2014_subclasses.conquest.scared-earth.su: In addition, the first time each turn that a creature moves into the area or starts its turn there, it takes 3d6 psychic damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.conquest.invincible-conq: At 20th level, you gain the ability to harness extraordinary martial prowess. As an action, you can magically become an avatar of conquest, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute: You have resistance to all damage. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as a part of that action. Your melee weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
At 20th level, you gain the ability to harness extraordinary martial prowess. (action).
2014_subclasses.oath-of-glory.descriptio: Paladins who take the Oath of Glory believe they and their companions are destined to achieve heroic glory through acts of courage, discipline, and deeds written in legend.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-glory.oath-spell: Gain oath spells at levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
3rd: Guiding Bolt, Heroism; 5th: Enhance Ability, Magic Weapon; 9th: Haste, Protection from Energy; 13th: Compulsion, Freedom of Movement; 17th: Commune, Flame Strike.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-glory.channel-di: Gain advantage on Athletics/Acrobatics checks, double carry weight, and jump distance +10 ft for 10 minutes.

As a bonus action, you can use your Channel Divinity to augment your athleticism. For 10 minutes, you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks; you can carry, push, drag, and lift twice as much weight; and your jump distance increases by 10 feet.
Distribute 2d8 + paladin level temporary hit points to allies within 30 feet after using Divine Smite.

Immediately after you deal damage to a creature with your Divine Smite feature, you can use your Channel Divinity as a bonus action to distribute temporary hit points to creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you (including yourself) equal to 2d8 + your paladin level, divided among them as you choose.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-glory.aura-of-al: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, and allies starting their turn within 5 feet (10 ft at 18th) gain +10 ft speed.

You exude an aura that fills you and your companions with vigor. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. In addition, that of each ally within 5 feet of you increases by 10 feet until the end of their next turn. At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 10 feet.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-glory.glorious-d: Reaction add your Charisma modifier to an ally's AC; if attack misses, make a weapon attack against the attacker.

You can turn defense into attack. When you or another creature you can see within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant a bonus to the target's AC against that attack equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). If the attack misses, you can immediately make one weapon attack against the attacker as part of this reaction, provided the attacker is within your weapon's range.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-glory.living-leg: Transform into a legendary hero for 1 minute: advantage on Charisma checks, reroll missed attacks, reaction spell save advantage.

You can empower yourself with the legends of your destiny. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute: you are blessed with an otherworldly presence, gaining advantage on all Charisma checks; once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack and miss, you can cause that attack to hit instead; and if you fail a saving throw, you can use your reaction to reroll it.
2014_subclasses.redemption.description: The Oath of Redemption sets a paladin on a difficult path, one that requires the courage to give quarter to those who have none and the strength to put mercy before justice.
2014_subclasses.redemption.channel-divin:
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following Channel Divinity options:

Emissary of Peace: As a bonus action, you grant a creature you can see within 30 feet of you a +5 bonus to its next Charisma check. The bonus lasts for 10 minutes.

Rebuke the Violent: When a creature within 30 feet of you deals damage to a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker takes radiant damage equal to the damage it just dealt. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
Rebuke the Violent: When a creature within 30 feet of you deals damage to a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to make.
2014_subclasses.redemption.aura-of-the-g: Starting at 7th level, you can shield others from harm. When a creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to magically take that damage, instead of that creature taking it. This feature doesn't transfer any other effects associated with the damage, and the damage can't be reduced in any way. At 18th level, the aura extends to 30 feet.
Can use your reaction to magically take that damage, instead of that creature taking it. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.redemption.protective-sp: Starting at 15th level, a protective, guardian spirit keeps you and your allies safe. If you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can use your reaction to grant a +5 bonus to the saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Can use your reaction to grant a +5 bonus to the saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.redemption.emissary-of-r: At 20th level, you become an avatar of peace, which gives you the following benefits: You have resistance to all damage dealt by other creatures (their attacks, spells, and other effects). Whenever a creature hits you with an attack, it takes radiant damage equal to half the damage you took from the attack. If you are reduced to 0 hit points by a creature and aren't killed outright, you can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Whenever a creature hits you with an attack, it takes radiant damage equal to half the damage you took from the attack. (action).
2014_subclasses.oath-of-the-crown.descri: The Oath of the Crown is sworn to the ideals of civilization, the law, and the preservation of an established sovereign realm.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-the-crown.oath-s: Gain oath spells at levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
3rd: Command, Compelled Duel; 5th: Warding Bond, Zone of Truth; 9th: Aura of Vitality, Spirit Guardians; 13th: Banishment, Guardian of Faith; 17th: Circle of Power, Geas.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-the-crown.channe: Force hostile creatures within 30 feet to stay within 30 feet of you on a failed Wisdom saving throw.

As a bonus action, you issue a challenge that compels other creatures to do battle with you. Each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature can't willingly move more than 30 feet away from you.
Restore 1d6 + Cha mod hit points to allies within 30 feet that have no more than half their max HP.

As a bonus action, you can bolster injured creatures with your Channel Divinity. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can hear you and has no more than half its hit points regains hit points equal to 1d6 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
2014_subclasses.oath-of-the-crown.divine: When an ally within 5 feet takes damage, use your reaction to magically take that damage instead.

Starting at 7th level, when a creature within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to magically substitute your own health for that of the target creature, taking that damage in its place. This damage to you cannot be reduced or prevented in any way.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-the-crown.unyiel: Gain advantage on saving throws to avoid being paralyzed or stunned.
Beginning at 15th level, you have advantage on saving throws to avoid becoming paralyzed or stunned.
2014_subclasses.oath-of-the-crown.exalte: For 1 hour: resistance to nonmagical weapon damage, allies within 30 ft have advantage on death and Wisdom saves.

At 20th level, your presence on the battlefield becomes an inspiration to your allies. As an action, you gain the following benefits for 1 hour: resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons; your allies within 30 feet have advantage on death saving throws; and you and your allies within 30 feet have advantage on Wisdom saving throws.
2014_subclasses.watchers.description: The Oath of the Watchers binds paladins to protect the mortal realm against otherworldly threats. These paladins are vigilant in spotting the influence of extraplanar entities and in defeating their agents.
2014_subclasses.watchers.channel-divinit:
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following Channel Divinity options:

Watcher's Will: As a bonus action, you grant yourself or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws for 1 minute.

Abjure the Extraplanar: As an action, you force each aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its save, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. Turned creatures must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving.
Abjure the Extraplanar: As an action, you force each aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw.
2014_subclasses.watchers.aura-of-the-sen: Starting at 7th level, you emit a 10-foot aura of alertness. If you and any creatures of your choice within the aura are sleeping, you and those creatures are not surprised when you wake up. In addition, you and creatures of your choice within the aura have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks. At 18th level, the aura extends to 30 feet.
Emit a 10-foot aura. You and creatures of your choice within the aura cannot be surprised while sleeping. At 18th level, the aura extends to 30 feet.
2014_subclasses.watchers.vigilant-rebuke: Starting at 15th level, you respond to threats with divine speed. When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll while under the effect of a spell or other magical effect, you can use your reaction to force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 3d8 psychic damage, and it has disadvantage on the attack roll. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage, and it doesn't suffer disadvantage on the attack roll.
Can use your reaction to force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. (reaction).
At 20th level, you channel divine power to protect the mortal realm. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute: You gain truesight with a range of 30 feet. You have advantage on attack rolls against aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey, and fiends. When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can turn the hit into a critical hit. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Have advantage on attack rolls against aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey, and fiends. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.description: An Oathbreaker is a paladin who has broken their sacred vows to pursue a dark ambition or serve a fiendish power. Only malice and dark magic remain where virtue once stood.
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.oathbreaker-: Gain dark oathbreaker spells at levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
3rd: Hellish Rebuke, Inflict Wounds; 5th: Crown of Madness, Darkness; 9th: Animate Dead, Bestow Curse; 13th: Blight, Confusion; 17th: Contagion, Dominate Person.
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.channel-divi: Take control of an undead creature within 30 feet with CR lower than your paladin level for 24 hours.

As an action, you target one undead creature you can see within 30 feet. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target must obey your commands for the next 24 hours, or until you use this Channel Divinity option again. An undead whose challenge rating is equal to or greater than your paladin level is immune.
Frighten all hostile creatures within 30 feet for 1 minute on a failed Wisdom saving throw.

As an action, the paladin channels the darkest emotions and focuses them into a burst of magical menace. Each creature of the paladin's choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw if it can see the paladin. On a failed save, the target is frightened of the paladin for 1 minute.
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.aura-of-hate: Add your Charisma modifier to melee weapon damage rolls for yourself and friendly fiends/undead within 10 ft.

Starting at 7th level, the paladin, as well as any fiends and undead within 10 feet of the paladin, gains a bonus to melee weapon damage rolls equal to the paladin's Charisma modifier (minimum of +1). At 18th level, the range increases to 30 feet.
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.supernatural: Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
At 15th level, the paladin gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.dread-lord.s: Transform into an avatar of darkness for 1 minute: 30 ft gloomy aura, 4d10 psychic damage, bonus action shadow attack.
2014_subclasses.oathbreaker.dread-lord.d: At 20th level, the paladin can surround himself or herself with an aura of gloom for 1 minute. The aura sheds dim light in a 30-foot radius. Enemies in the aura take 4d10 psychic damage at the start of their turns if frightened, and the paladin can use a bonus action to make a melee spell attack dealing 3d10 + Cha necrotic damage.
2014_subclasses.vengeance.description:
The Oath of Vengeance represents the power of righteous fury and retribution. Paladins who swear this oath are typically driven by a personal quest for revenge against evil.

They are willing to sometimes circumvent conventional morality to defeat evil, and they do not show mercy to those who have committed evil acts. Their oath is a solemn vow to pursue and destroy the wicked, no matter the cost.
2014_subclasses.vengeance.oath-spells.de:
Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.
2014_subclasses.vengeance.oath-spells.su: Gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description.
2014_subclasses.vengeance.channel-divini: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer of denunciation, using your Channel Divinity. Choose one creature within 60 feet of you that you can see. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw, unless it is immune to being frightened. Fiends and undead have disadvantage on this saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is frightened for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While frightened, the creature's speed is 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed. On a successful save, the creature's speed is halved for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.
Choose one creature within 60 feet of you that you can see. (action).

As a bonus action, you can utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 10 feet of you, using your Channel Divinity. You gain advantage on attack rolls against the creature for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious.
Can utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 10 feet of you, using your Channel Divinity. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.vengeance.relentless-ave: By 7th level, your supernatural focus helps you close off a foe's retreat. When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you can move up to half your speed immediately after the attack and as part of the same reaction. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
Can move up to half your speed immediately after the attack and as part of the same reaction. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.vengeance.soul-of-vengea: Starting at 15th level, the authority with which you speak your Vow of Enmity gives you greater power over your foe. When a creature under the effect of your Vow of Enmity makes an attack, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature if it is within range.
Can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature if it is within range. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.vengeance.avenging-angel: At 20th level, you can assume the form of an angelic avenger. Using your action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 hour, you gain the following benefits: Wings sprout from your back and grant you a flying speed of 60 feet. You emanate an aura of menace in a 30-foot radius. The first time any enemy creature enters the aura or starts its turn there during a battle, the creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. Attack rolls against the frightened creature have advantage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Gain the following benefits: Wings sprout from your back and grant you a flying speed of 60 feet. (action).
2014_subclasses.beast-master.description:
The Beast Master archetype embodies a friendship between the civilized races and the beasts of the world. United in focus, beast and ranger work as one to fight the monstrous foes that threaten civilization and the wilderness alike.

Emulating the Beast Master archetype means committing yourself to this ideal, working in partnership with an animal as its companion and friend. The bond between a Beast Master and their companion is unbreakable, forged through shared battles and mutual trust.
2014_subclasses.beast-master.ranger-s-co: At 3rd level, you gain a beast companion that accompanies you on your adventures and is trained to fight alongside you. Choose a beast that is no larger than Medium and that has a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower. Add your proficiency bonus to the beast's AC, attack rolls, and damage rolls, as well as to any saving throws and skills it is proficient in. Its hit point maximum equals its normal maximum or four times your ranger level, whichever is higher. The beast obeys your commands as best as it can. It takes its turn on your initiative. On your turn, you can verbally command the beast where to move (no action required by you). You can use your action to verbally command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, or Help action. If you don't issue a command, the beast takes the Dodge action. Once you have the Extra Attack feature, you can make one weapon attack yourself when you command the beast to take the Attack action. If you are incapacitated or absent, the beast acts on its own, focusing on protecting you and itself. The beast never requires your command to use its reaction. If the beast dies, you can obtain another one by spending 8 hours magically bonding with another beast that isn't hostile to you, either the same type of beast as before or a different one.
Add your proficiency bonus to the beast's AC, attack rolls, and damage rolls, as well as to any saving throws and skills it is proficient in. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.beast-master.exceptional: Beginning at 7th level, on any of your turns when your beast companion doesn't attack, you can use a bonus action to command the beast to take the Dash, Disengage, or Help action on its turn. In addition, the beast's attacks now count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
In addition, the beast's attacks now count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.beast-master.bestial-fur: Starting at 11th level, when you command your beast companion to take the Attack action, the beast can make two attacks, or it can take the Multiattack action if it has that action.
Starting at 11th level, when you command your beast companion to take the Attack action, the beast can make two attacks, or it can take the Multiattack action if it.
2014_subclasses.beast-master.share-spell: Beginning at 15th level, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your beast companion with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.
Beginning at 15th level, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your beast companion with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.
2014_subclasses.drake-warden.description: Drake Wardens are rangers who have bonded with a lesser drake, forming a mystical connection with their draconic companion. These rangers train alongside their drake, learning to fight as one with their scaled ally.
2014_subclasses.drake-warden.draconic-gi: You gain a drake companion that accompanies you on your adventures. The drake is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See the Drake Companion stat block for its traits and actions. In combat, the drake shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it can take is the Dodge action, unless you use your bonus action on your turn to command it to take an action.
Gain a drake companion that accompanies you on your adventures. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.drake-warden.bond-of-fan: Your drake's bond with you grants it resilience. While your drake is within 30 feet of you, it has a +2 bonus to AC and saving throws.
While your drake is within 30 feet of you, it has a +2 bonus to AC and saving throws.
2014_subclasses.drake-warden.drake-s-bre: As an action, you can command your drake to exhale a 15-foot cone of elemental energy. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier). On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 damage of the type associated with your drake. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 damage of the type associated with your drake. (action).
2014_subclasses.drake-warden.perfected-b: Your bond with your drake deepens. When you take damage while your drake is within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to have your drake take the damage instead. Additionally, when you deal damage to a creature within 30 feet of your drake, you can have your drake make a bite attack against that creature as a reaction.
Additionally, when you deal damage to a creature within 30 feet of your drake, you can have your drake make a bite attack against that creature as a reaction. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.drake-warden.reflexive-r: When you or your drake takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage type to both you and your drake for 1 minute. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage type to both you and your drake for 1 minute. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.description: Fey Wanderers are rangers who have learned to tap into the magic of the Feywild. They are adept at traversing the border between the mortal world and the realm of the fey, and they use their connection to the fey to bolster their own abilities and those of their allies.
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.dreadful-st: At 3rd level, you can use your connection to the Feywild to mark your foes with otherworldly dread. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d4 psychic damage to the target. The damage increases to 1d6 at 11th level.
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d4 psychic damage to the target. (action).
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.fey-wandere:
At 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Fey Wanderer Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

3rd: charm person
5th: misty step
9th: dispel magic
13th: dimension door
17th: mislead
The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.otherworldl: At 3rd level, your fey connection allows you to project a magical glamour. When you make a Charisma check, you can expend a use of this feature to gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1). You can also use this feature on a Charisma (Deception), Charisma (Intimidation), or Charisma (Performance) check.
Can expend a use of this feature to gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1). (action).
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.beguiling-t: Starting at 7th level, the magic of the Feywild safeguards your mind. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened. In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against being charmed or frightened, you can use your reaction to force a different creature you can see within 120 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. If the save fails, the target is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.
In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against being charmed or frightened, you can use your reaction.
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.fey-reinfor: At 11th level, the royal courts of the Feywild have noticed you. Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that summons a fey or a beast, the summoned creature gains the following benefits: The creature appears with more hit points than normal: 1 extra hit point per level of the spell. The summoned creature's weapon attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
The summoned creature's weapon attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
2014_subclasses.fey-wanderer.misty-wande: At 15th level, you can use the mystical energy of the Feywild to move between planes. Once per short rest, you can cast the misty step spell, requiring no spell slot or material components. In addition, when you use this feature, you can bring along up to two willing creatures within 5 feet of you, provided you have a way to reach them (such as a rope or chain).
In addition, when you use this feature, you can bring along up to two willing creatures within 5 feet of you, provided you have a way to reach them.
2014_subclasses.gloom-stalker.descriptio: Gloom Stalkers are at home in the darkest places: deep under the earth, in shadowy alleyways, and in primeval forests. They master the shadows to ambush threats before enemies even know they are there.
2014_subclasses.gloom-stalker.gloom-stal: Gain additional spells at levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
3rd: Disguise Self; 5th: Rope Trick; 9th: Fear; 13th: Greater Invisibility; 17th: Seeming.
2014_subclasses.gloom-stalker.dread-ambu: Add Wisdom modifier to initiative, gain +10 ft speed on your first turn, and make an extra attack dealing +1d8 damage.

At 3rd level, you master the art of the ambush. You can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Wisdom modifier. At the start of your first turn of each combat, your walking speed increases by 10 feet, which lasts until the end of that turn. If you take the Attack action on that turn, you can make one additional weapon attack as part of that action. If that attack hits, the target takes an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's damage type.
2014_subclasses.gloom-stalker.umbral-sig: Gain 60 ft darkvision (or +30 ft), and become completely invisible to any creature relying on darkvision in darkness.

At 3rd level, you gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision from your race, its range increases by 30 feet. You are also adept at evading creatures that rely on darkvision. While in darkness, you are invisible to any creature that relies on darkvision to see you in that darkness.
Gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws (or Intelligence or Charisma if you already have it).

By 7th level, you have honed your ability to resist the mind-altering powers of your prey. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).
2014_subclasses.gloom-stalker.stalker-s-: Once on each of your turns when you miss with a weapon attack, make another weapon attack as part of the same action.

At 11th level, you learn to attack with such rapid speed that you can turn a miss into another strike. Once on each of your turns when you miss with a weapon attack, you can make another weapon attack as part of the same action.
2014_subclasses.gloom-stalker.shadowy-do: Impose disadvantage on an attack roll against you as a reaction unless the attacker has advantage.

Starting at 15th level, you can dodge in unforeseen ways, with wisps of supernatural shadow around you. Whenever a creature makes an attack roll against you and doesn't have advantage on the roll, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on it.
2014_subclasses.horizon-walker.descripti: Rangers who walk the border between planes are known as Horizon Wanderers. They are adept at hunting creatures that cross between worlds, and they use their knowledge of the planes to protect the mortal realm.
2014_subclasses.horizon-walker.detect-po: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to magically sense the presence of a planar portal. As an action, you can detect the distance and direction to the closest planar portal within 1 mile of you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
At 3rd level, you gain the ability to magically sense the presence of a planar portal. (action).
2014_subclasses.horizon-walker.planar-wa: At 3rd level, you learn to draw on the energy of other planes to enhance your attacks. As a bonus action, you can choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The next time you hit that creature on this turn with a weapon attack, all damage dealt by the attack becomes force damage, and the target takes an extra 1d8 force damage from the attack. When you reach 11th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.
The next time you hit that creature on this turn with a weapon attack, all damage dealt by the attack becomes force damage, and the target takes an extra 1d8.
2014_subclasses.horizon-walker.ethereal-: At 7th level, you learn to step through the Ethereal Plane. As a bonus action, you can cast the etherealness spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the spell ends at the end of your current turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Can cast the etherealness spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the spell ends at the end of your current turn. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.horizon-walker.distant-s: At 11th level, you gain the ability to pass between the planes in the midst of battle. When you take the Attack action, you can teleport up to 10 feet before each attack to an unoccupied space you can see. If you attack at least two different creatures with the action, you can make one additional weapon attack with it.
Can teleport up to 10 feet before each attack to an unoccupied space you can see. (action).
2014_subclasses.horizon-walker.spectral-: At 15th level, your ability to move between planes enables you to slip away from harm. When you take damage from an attack, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to all of that attack's damage.
At 15th level, your ability to move between planes enables you to slip away from harm. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.hunter.description: Emulating the Hunter archetype means accepting your place as a bulwark between civilization and the terrors of the wilderness. As you walk the Hunter's path, you learn specialized techniques for fighting the threats you face, from rampaging ogres and hordes of orcs to towering giants and terrifying dragons.
2014_subclasses.hunter.hunter-s-prey.des:
At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Colossus Slayer
Giant Killer
Horde Breaker
2014_subclasses.hunter.hunter-s-prey.sum: Choose one: Colossus Slayer (extra 1d8 damage once per turn), Giant Killer (use reaction to attack when a Large or larger creature hits you), or Horde Breaker (make an extra attack against a different creature within 5 feet of the target).
2014_subclasses.hunter.defensive-tactics:
At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Escape the Horde
Multiattack Defense
Steel Will

Choose one: Escape the Horde (opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage), Multiattack Defense (when hit by an attack, gain +4 AC against the attacker until the end of your next turn), or Steel Will (advantage on saving throws against being frightened).
2014_subclasses.hunter.multiattack.descr:
At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Volley
Whirlwind Attack
2014_subclasses.hunter.multiattack.summa: Choose one: Volley (use your action to make a ranged attack against every creature within 10 feet of a point you can see within range) or Whirlwind Attack (make a melee attack against every creature within 5 feet of you).
2014_subclasses.hunter.superior-hunter-s:
At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Evasion
Stand Against the Tide
Uncanny Dodge

Choose one: Evasion (take no damage on a successful Dexterity saving throw against an effect), Stand Against the Tide (use reaction to redirect a missed attack to another creature), or Uncanny Dodge (use reaction to halve the damage of an attack).
2014_subclasses.monster-slayer.descripti: Rangers who dedicate themselves to hunting and slaying monsters are known as Monster Slayers. They are skilled in tracking their prey and in using their knowledge of monsters to defeat them.
2014_subclasses.monster-slayer.hunter-s-: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to peer at a creature and magically discern how best to hurt it. As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You immediately learn whether the creature has any damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities and what they are. If the creature is hidden from divination magic, you sense that it is present, but you learn nothing about its defenses.
Choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. (action).
2014_subclasses.monster-slayer.slayer-s-: At 3rd level, you can target a creature for death. As a bonus action, you designate one creature you can see within 60 feet of you as your slayer's prey. The first time each turn you hit that target with a weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d6 damage to it. This benefit lasts until you finish a short or long rest. When you finish a rest, you can transfer the benefit to a different creature when you spot the creature within 60 feet of you, provided you aren't incapacitated.
The first time each turn you hit that target with a weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d6 damage to it. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.monster-slayer.supernatu: At 7th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to any saving throw you make that doesn't already include your Wisdom modifier. In addition, you gain a +1 bonus to your AC while you are not wearing heavy armor.
At 7th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to any saving throw you make that doesn't already include your Wisdom modifier.
2014_subclasses.monster-slayer.magic-use: At 11th level, you gain the ability to thwart someone else's spellcasting. When you see a creature casting a spell or using a magical effect within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a Wisdom check, with a DC of 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the creature's spell fails and has no effect, and any material components used to cast the spell are wasted. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Can use your reaction to make a Wisdom check, with a DC of 10 + the spell's level. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.monster-slayer.slayer-s-: At 15th level, you gain the ability to counterattack when your prey tries to resist your assault. If the target of your Slayer's Prey forces you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against the creature. You make this attack immediately before making the saving throw. If your attack hits, your saving throw against the target's effect is made with advantage.
Make this attack immediately before making the saving throw. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.swarmkeeper.description: Swarmkeepers are rangers who have learned to call upon the power of nature's smallest creatures. They can summon a swarm of fey spirits that take the form of various creatures, and they use the swarm to aid them in battle.
2014_subclasses.swarmkeeper.swarmkeeper-:
At 3rd level, you learn the mage hand cantrip if you don't already know it. When you cast it, the hand takes the form of a swarm of nature spirits. In addition, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Swarmkeeper Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

3rd: faerie fire
5th: web
9th: gaseous form
13th: giant insect
17th: insect plague
The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.
2014_subclasses.swarmkeeper.gathered-swa:
At 3rd level, you can call forth a swarm of fey spirits to attack your enemies. As a bonus action, you can conjure the swarm in a space you can see within 30 feet of you. The swarm is a spectral version of a Tiny beast (bats, insects, birds, or other creatures of your choice). The swarm occupies its space and doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. The swarm remains for 1 minute, until you dismiss it as a bonus action, or until you use this feature again.

When you conjure the swarm, you can choose one of the following effects:

Damage: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can have the swarm deal 1d6 piercing, slashing, or bludgeoning damage (your choice) to the target.

Movement: You can use a bonus action to move the swarm up to 30 feet. If the swarm moves through a creature's space, that creature takes 1 piercing damage. You can also move a willing creature within 5 feet of the swarm up to 10 feet.

Protection: When a creature you can see takes damage while within 5 feet of the swarm, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d6.

The damage increases to 2d6 at 11th level.
Protection: When a creature you can see takes damage while within 5 feet of the swarm, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d6. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.swarmkeeper.writhing-tid: At 7th level, you can call on the swarm to lift you up. As a bonus action, you gain a flying speed of 10 feet. This speed lasts for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
As a bonus action, gain a flying speed of 10 feet for 1 minute or until incapacitated. Usable a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.
2014_subclasses.swarmkeeper.mighty-swarm:
At 11th level, your Gathered Swarm grows more powerful. When you use Gathered Swarm, you can choose one of the following additional benefits:

Damage: The swarm's damage increases by 1d6.

Movement: The swarm's movement speed increases by10 feet, and the creature moved takes 1d6 damage.

Protection: The damage reduction increases by 1d6.
Movement: The swarm's movement speed increases by10 feet, and the creature moved takes 1d6 damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.swarmkeeper.swarming-dis: At 15th level, you can call on the swarm to protect you from harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to that damage type until the end of the current turn. The swarm then teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you.
The swarm then teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.arcane-trickster.descrip:
Some rogues enhance their fine-honed skills of stealth and agility with magic, learning tricks of enchantment and illusion. These rogues include pickpockets and burglars, but also pranksters, mischief-makers, and a significant number of adventurers.

You learn to cast spells, typically spells of enchantment and illusion, to augment your existing abilities. You also learn to use your mage hand to perform tricks at range, picking pockets and disarm traps from a distance.
2014_subclasses.arcane-trickster.spellca: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells. Cantrips: You learn three cantrips: mage hand and two other cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn another wizard cantrip of your choice at 10th level. Spell Slots: The Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your wizard spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest. Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher: You know three 1st-level spells of your choice from the wizard spell list. The Spells Known column of the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table shows when you learn more wizard spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the wizard spells you know and replace it with another spell from the wizard spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots. Spellcasting Ability: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your wizard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one. Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.
In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
2014_subclasses.arcane-trickster.mage-ha: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast mage hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and you can perform the following additional tasks with it: You can stow one object the hand is holding in a container worn or carried by another creature. You can retrieve an object in a container worn or carried by another creature. You can use thieves' tools to pick locks and disarm traps at range. You can perform one of these tasks without being noticed by a creature if you succeed on a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by the creature's Wisdom (Perception) check. In addition, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to control the hand.
Can retrieve an object in a container worn or carried by another creature. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.arcane-trickster.magical: Starting at 9th level, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.
Starting at 9th level, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against.
2014_subclasses.arcane-trickster.versati: At 13th level, you gain the ability to distract targets with your mage hand. As a bonus action on your turn, you can designate a creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand created by the spell. You have advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.
Can designate a creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand created by the spell. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.arcane-trickster.spell-t: At 17th level, you gain the ability to magically steal knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster. When a creature casts a spell of 1st level or higher within 60 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to force the spellcaster to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to your spell save DC). On a failed save, you learn the spell if it is of a level for which you have spell slots. The spellcaster loses the spell if they cast it at 3rd level or lower. The spell remains in effect if the spellcaster succeeds on the saving throw. Once you successfully steal a spell using this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Can use your reaction to force the spellcaster to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to your spell save DC). (reaction).
2014_subclasses.assassin.description:
You focus your training on the grim art of death. Those who adhere to this archetype are diverse: hired killers, spies, bounty hunters, and even specially anointed priests trained to exterminate the enemies of their deity.

You have a powerful advantage when you can strike from the shadows, taking your foe unawares. You are a master of disguise, poison, and deception, using your skills to eliminate targets with ruthless efficiency.
2014_subclasses.assassin.bonus-proficien: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
Gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.
2014_subclasses.assassin.assassinate.des: Starting at 3rd level, you are at your deadliest when you get the drop on your enemies. You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn in the combat yet. In addition, any hit you score against a creature that is surprised is a critical hit.
2014_subclasses.assassin.assassinate.sum: Have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn in the combat yet. (action).
2014_subclasses.assassin.infiltration-ex: Starting at 9th level, you can unfailingly create false identities for yourself. You must spend seven days and 25 gp to establish a new identity, including establishing history, contacts, and appropriate credentials. You can't establish an identity that belongs to someone else. Thereafter, other creatures believe you are that person until given an obvious reason not to.
Starting at 9th level, you can unfailingly create false identities for yourself. (action).
2014_subclasses.assassin.impostor.descri: At 13th level, you acquire the ability to unearth another creature's speech, handwriting, or both, given three hours of study. Your ruse is indiscernible to the untrained eye. However, a creature that is suspicious of you can make a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check to determine that you are not who you claim to be.
2014_subclasses.assassin.impostor.summar: You acquire the ability to unearth another creature's speech, handwriting, or both, given three hours of study.
2014_subclasses.assassin.death-strike.de: Starting at 17th level, you become a master of instant death. When you attack and hit a creature that is surprised, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, you double the damage of your attack against the creature.
2014_subclasses.assassin.death-strike.su: It must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus).
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.description: Inquisitives are specialist sleuths who use their knowledge of body language and psychology to detect lies and ferret out secrets. They are often employed by nobles, merchants, and law enforcement to investigate crimes and uncover the truth.
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.ear-for-dece: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you develop a keen ear for deception. Whenever you make a Wisdom (Insight) check to determine whether someone is lying or to get a hunch about a person's manner, you can treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8.
Whenever you make a Wisdom (Insight) check to determine whether someone is lying or to get a hunch about a person's manner, you can treat a d20 roll of 7.
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.eye-for-deta: Starting at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check to spot a hidden object or creature, or to make an Investigation check to uncover or decipher clues. In addition, you can use a bonus action to make a Wisdom (Insight) check to get a hunch about a person's manner.
Use a bonus action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check to spot a hidden object or creature, or to make an Investigation check.
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.insightful-f: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to read a foe's fighting style and exploit its weaknesses. As a bonus action, you can make a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by the target's Charisma (Deception) check. If you win the contest, you can use your Sneak Attack against that target even if you don't have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage. This benefit lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature against a different creature.
Can use your Sneak Attack against that target even if you don't have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.steady-eye.d: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Insight) check that relies on your sight when you, the target you are trying to observe, and your observer are all in the same plane of existence. In addition, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight when you are not moving.
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.steady-eye.s: You have advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Insight) check that relies on your sight when you, the target you.
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.unerring-eye: At 13th level, your ability to read the intentions of others becomes nearly supernatural. As an action, you can sense the presence of shapechangers and anything that isn't in its original form, and you can detect the presence of illusions and other magic that masks the true form of a creature or object within 30 feet of you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Can sense the presence of shapechangers and anything that isn't in its original form, and you can detect the presence of illusions and other magic that masks the true form.
2014_subclasses.inquisitive.eye-for-weak: Starting at 17th level, you learn to exploit a creature's weaknesses by studying its tactics. While your Insightful Fighting feature applies to a creature, your Sneak Attack damage against that creature increases by 3d6.
Your Sneak Attack damage against that creature increases by 3d6.
2014_subclasses.mastermind.description: Masterminds are criminal masterminds who use their cunning and charisma to manipulate others. They are often the brains behind criminal enterprises, and they use their knowledge of the law and their connections to stay one step ahead of the authorities.
2014_subclasses.mastermind.master-of-int: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the disguise kit, the forgery kit, and one gaming set of your choice. You also learn two languages of your choice. You can mimic the speech of another person or the sounds made by other creatures. You must have heard the person speaking, or heard the creature make the noise, for at least 1 minute. A successful Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check allows a listener to determine that the effect is faked.
Gain proficiency with the disguise kit, the forgery kit, and one gaming set of your choice. (action).
2014_subclasses.mastermind.master-of-tac: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the Help action as a bonus action. Additionally, when you use the Help action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you, rather than within 5 feet of you.
Additionally, when you use the Help action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you, rather than within.
2014_subclasses.mastermind.insightful-ma: Starting at 9th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if your target is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice: Intelligence score, Wisdom score, Charisma score, Class levels (if any).
Starting at 9th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your.
At 13th level, you can sometimes cause another creature to take the blow meant for you. When you are targeted by an attack while a creature within 5 feet of you is granting you cover against that attack, you can use your reaction to have the attack target that creature instead of you.
Can use your reaction to have the attack target that creature instead of you. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.mastermind.soul-of-decei: Starting at 17th level, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means, unless you allow it. You can present false thoughts by succeeding on a Charisma (Deception) check contested by the mind reader's Wisdom (Insight) check. Additionally, no matter what you say, magic that would determine if you are telling the truth indicates that you are being truthful, if you so choose, and you can't be compelled to tell the truth by magic.
Starting at 17th level, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means, unless you allow it. (action).
2014_subclasses.phantom.description: Many rogues walk a fine line between life and death. Phantoms embrace that connection, drawing on the knowledge and whispers of spirits to walk between worlds.
2014_subclasses.phantom.whispers-of-the-: Echoes of the dead grant you proficiency in one skill or tool of your choice each short or long rest.

Echoes of those who have died begin to cling to you. Whenever you finish a short or long rest, you can choose one skill or tool proficiency that you lack and gain it, as a ghostly presence shares its knowledge with you. You lose this proficiency when you use this feature to choose a different proficiency.
2014_subclasses.phantom.wails-from-the-g: When you deal Sneak Attack damage, deal half your Sneak Attack dice in necrotic damage to a second creature within 30 ft.

As you nudge someone closer to the grave, you can channel the wails of departed spirits. Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature on your turn, you can target a second creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature. Roll half the number of Sneak Attack dice for your level (round up), and the second creature takes necrotic damage equal to the roll's total.
2014_subclasses.phantom.tokens-of-the-de: Snatch the soul of a dying creature within 30 ft into a Soul Trinket granting advantage on Death and Con saves.

When a creature dies within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to capture its soul into a tiny trinket called a soul trinket (max up to your proficiency bonus). While carrying a soul trinket, you have advantage on death saving throws and Constitution saving throws. You can destroy a trinket to ask the spirit a question or use Wails from the Grave without expending a use.
2014_subclasses.phantom.ghost-walk.summa: Transform into a ghostly form for 10 minutes: 10 ft flying speed, disadvantage on attacks against you, and pass through solid objects.
2014_subclasses.phantom.ghost-walk.descr: You can phase, at least partially, into the realm of the dead. As a bonus action, you assume a spectral form for 10 minutes (or until dismissed). You gain a flying speed of 10 feet and can hover; attack rolls against you have disadvantage; and you can move through creatures and solid objects as if they were difficult terrain.
2014_subclasses.phantom.death-s-friend.s: Wails from the Grave deals damage to both targets, and gain a free soul trinket at the end of a long rest.
