2014_subclasses.phantom.death-s-friend.d: Your association with death reaches its peak: when you use your Wails from the Grave, you can now deal the necrotic damage to both the first and the second creature. In addition, whenever you finish a long rest, a soul trinket appears in your hand if you don't already have one.
2014_subclasses.scout.description: Skirmishers are skirmishers who excel at scouting ahead of the main group. They are skilled in stealth, tracking, and survival, and they use their knowledge of the wilderness to aid their allies.
2014_subclasses.scout.skirmisher.descrip: Starting at 3rd level, you are difficult to pin down during a fight. You can move up to half your speed as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
2014_subclasses.scout.skirmisher.summary: Can move up to half your speed as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.scout.survivalist.descri: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Nature and Survival skills if you don't already have them. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those proficiencies.
2014_subclasses.scout.survivalist.summar: Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those proficiencies. (action).
At 9th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet. If you are wearing medium or heavy armor, this bonus is reduced to 5 feet.
At 9th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
2014_subclasses.scout.ambush-master.desc: At 13th level, you excel at setting ambushes. When you use the Hide action during combat, you can make a Dexterity (Stealth) check with advantage. In addition, if you are hidden from a creature when you make an attack roll against it, you have advantage on the attack roll.
2014_subclasses.scout.ambush-master.summ: In addition, if you are hidden from a creature when you make an attack roll against it, you have advantage on the attack roll. (action).
2014_subclasses.scout.sudden-strike.desc: Starting at 17th level, you can strike with deadly speed. If you use the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as a bonus action. This attack can use your Sneak Attack even if you already used it this turn, but you can't use your Sneak Attack on both attacks against the same target.
2014_subclasses.scout.sudden-strike.summ: Starting at 17th level, you can strike with deadly speed. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.soulknife.description: Soulknives strike and infiltrate with the power of their minds. They manifest blades of shimmering psychic energy from their hands to execute stealthy assassinations and bridge thoughts with allies.
Harbor Psionic Energy dice (d6s scaling to d12s) to fuel Psi-Bolstered Knack and Psychic Whispers.

You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself, represented by your Psionic Energy dice (twice your proficiency bonus in d6s, scaling to d8 at 5th, d10 at 11th, and d12 at 17th level). You can use your dice for: Psi-Bolstered Knack (add the die to a failed ability check using a proficient skill; if it still fails, the die is not expended) and Psychic Whispers (telepathically connect with allies within 1 mile for hours equal to the die roll).
2014_subclasses.soulknife.psychic-blades: Manifest shimmering blades of psychic energy dealing 1d6 psychic damage, with a 1d4 bonus action offhand strike.

You can manifest your psionic power as shimmering blades of psychic energy. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can manifest a psychic blade from your free hand and make the attack with that blade. It is a simple melee weapon with the finesse and thrown properties (range 60 ft). It deals 1d6 psychic damage on a hit. If you attack with a blade, you can use a bonus action to make a second psychic blade attack with your other hand, dealing 1d4 psychic damage.
2014_subclasses.soulknife.soul-blades.su: Expend Psionic Energy dice to boost missed psychic blade attack rolls or teleport up to 10x the roll in feet.
2014_subclasses.soulknife.soul-blades.de: You can weave your psychic blades with your psionic power in two new ways: Homing Strikes (if you miss with a psychic blade, add a Psionic Energy die to the attack roll; die is expended only if the attack hits) and Psychic Teleportation (bonus action throw a blade up to 10 times the number rolled on a Psionic Energy die in feet and teleport to that unoccupied space).
2014_subclasses.soulknife.psychic-veil.s: Become completely invisible for 1 hour as an action; ends if you deal damage or force a saving throw.
2014_subclasses.soulknife.psychic-veil.d: You can weave a veil of psychic static to mask your physical presence. As an action, you can magically become invisible, along with anything you are wearing or carrying, for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect. The invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature or you force a creature to make a saving throw. You can use this once per long rest, or by expending a Psionic Energy die.
2014_subclasses.soulknife.rend-mind.summ: When you deal Sneak Attack damage with a psychic blade, force a Wisdom save or stun the target for 1 minute.
2014_subclasses.soulknife.rend-mind.desc: You can sweep your psychic blade directly through a creature's mind. When you use your Psychic Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier). If the save fails, the target is stunned for 1 minute. The stunned target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.description: Swashbucklers are charismatic duelists who rely on charm and wit as much as they do on their blades. They are often found in the courts of nobles, where they use their skills to navigate the treacherous waters of politics and intrigue.
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.fancy-footw: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to land a strike and then escape retaliation. During your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can't make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of your turn.
During your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can't make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of your turn. (action).
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.rakish-auda: Starting at 3rd level, your confidence propels you into battle. You can give yourself advantage on a Charisma (Persuasion) check if you have not yet done so this encounter. In addition, you don't need advantage on your attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a creature if you are within 5 feet of it, no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. All the other rules for Sneak Attack still apply to you.
In addition, you don't need advantage on your attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a creature if you are within 5 feet of it, no other creatures.
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.panache.des: At 9th level, your charm becomes exceedingly persuasive. As an action, you can make a Charisma (Persuasion) check contested by a creature's Charisma (Intimidation) check. The creature must be able to hear you, and you must share a language with it. If you succeed, the creature is charmed by you for 1 minute. While charmed, the creature is friendly to you and your allies. If you fail, the creature is immune to your Panache for 24 hours.
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.panache.sum: The creature is immune to your Panache for 24 hours. (action).
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.elegant-man: Starting at 13th level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to gain advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check you make during the same turn.
Starting at 13th level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to gain advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check you make during the same.
2014_subclasses.swashbuckler.duelist-s-d: Starting at 17th level, your mastery of the blade allows you to turn defense into offense. When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss.
Can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.thief.description: You hone your skills in the larcenous arts. Burglars, bandits, cutpurses, and other criminals typically follow this archetype, but so do rogues who prefer to think of themselves as professional treasure seekers, explorers, delvers, and investigators. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you learn skills useful for delving into ancient ruins, reading unfamiliar languages, and using magic items you normally couldn't employ.
2014_subclasses.thief.fast-hands.descrip: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.
2014_subclasses.thief.fast-hands.summary: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm.
When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.
Gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement. (action).
2014_subclasses.thief.supreme-sneak.desc: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
2014_subclasses.thief.supreme-sneak.summ: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
2014_subclasses.thief.use-magic-device.d: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.
2014_subclasses.thief.use-magic-device.s: Ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items. (action).
2014_subclasses.thief.thief-s-reflexes.d: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.
2014_subclasses.thief.thief-s-reflexes.s: Take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. (action).
2014_subclasses.aberrant-mind.descriptio: An alien influence has wrapped its tendrils around your mind, giving you psionic power. You can now project that power to alter the world around you. You can also use your psionic power to cast spells.
At 1st level, you can use your action to touch a willing creature's mind and establish a telepathic link with it. Until the effect ends, you and the creature can share words, images, sounds, and other sensory messages with one another through the link. The link is broken if you and the creature are on different planes of existence or if either of you is incapacitated. The creature must be able to understand at least one language.
Until the effect ends, you and the creature can share words, images, sounds, and other sensory messages with one another through the link. (action).
2014_subclasses.aberrant-mind.psionic-sp:
Starting at 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Psionic Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of sorcerer spells you know.

1st: arms of Hadar, dissonant whispers, mind sliver
3rd: calm emotions, detect thoughts, hunger of Hadar
5th: compulsion, Sending, slow
7th: Evard's black tentacles, summon aberration
9th: Rary's telepathic bond, telekinesis
11th: psychic scream, summon aberration
Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of sorcerer spells you know.
2014_subclasses.aberrant-mind.psychic-de: At 6th level, you can use your mind to deflect attacks. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to roll 1d4 and add it to your AC until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering attack. When you use this feature, you can also choose to either gain advantage on the next attack roll you make before the end of your next turn, or impose disadvantage on the next attack roll made against you before the end of your next turn.
Can use your reaction to roll 1d4 and add it to your AC until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering attack. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.aberrant-mind.revelation:
Starting at 14th level, you can unleash the aberrant truth hidden within your flesh. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more sorcery points to magically transform your body for 1 minute. For each point you spend, you gain one of the following benefits of your choice, the benefits lasting until the transformation ends:

You can see any invisible creature within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover.

You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, and you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings, while leaving your hands free.

You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe underwater.

Your eyes become a deeper color, and you can see in darkness (both dim light and darkness) to a range of 60 feet.
Gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe underwater. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.aberrant-mind.warping-im: At 18th level, you can warp space around a creature to destroy it. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 120 feet of you. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 5d10 force damage and is teleported to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't teleported. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 hit points, it is disintegrated. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
On a failed save, the creature takes 5d10 force damage and is teleported to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you. (action).
2014_subclasses.clockwork-soul.descripti: The cosmic power of Mechanus and the clockwork gears of order infuse your soul. You weave magic that corrects balance, removes advantage and disadvantage, and protects reality from chaos.
2014_subclasses.clockwork-soul.clockwork: Learn additional order and abjuration spells at levels 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.

1st: Alarm, Protection from Evil and Good; 3rd: Aid, Lesser Restoration; 5th: Dispel Magic, Protection from Energy; 7th: Freedom of Movement, Summon Construct; 9th: Greater Restoration, Wall of Force. You can replace these with abjuration or transmutation spells from the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell lists.
2014_subclasses.clockwork-soul.restore-b: Reaction cancel advantage or disadvantage on a d20 roll for a creature within 60 feet.

Your connection to the plane of absolute law allows you to equalize chaotic fluctuations. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is about to roll a d20 with advantage or disadvantage, you can use your reaction to prevent the roll from being affected by advantage and disadvantage.
2014_subclasses.clockwork-soul.bastion-o: Spend 1 to 5 sorcery points to create a protective ward of d8s that reduces incoming damage.

You can imbue a creature with a shimmering shield of order. As an action, you can expend 1 to 5 sorcery points to create a magical ward around yourself or another creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The ward has a number of d8s equal to the sorcery points spent. When the warded creature takes damage, it can expend a number of those dice, roll them, and reduce the damage taken by the total rolled.
2014_subclasses.clockwork-soul.trance-of: Enter a clockwork trance for 1 minute: attacks against you can't have advantage, and attack/check/save d20 rolls of 9 or lower count as 10.

As a bonus action, you can enter a state of clockwork perfection for 1 minute. Attack rolls against you can't benefit from advantage, and whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10.
2014_subclasses.clockwork-soul.clockwork: Summon a 30-foot cube of clockwork spirits: restore up to 100 HP, repair broken objects, and end 6th level or lower spells.

You summon a procession of spirits of order to restore balance. As an action, you summon spirits in a 30-foot cube originating from you: the spirits restore up to 100 hit points, divided as you choose among any number of creatures in the cube; damaged objects in the cube are instantly repaired; and any spells of 6th level or lower on creatures and objects in the cube end.
2014_subclasses.divine-soul.description: A divine soul has been touched by the grace of a divine being. The magic you wield is a gift from the gods, and you are a conduit for their power.
2014_subclasses.divine-soul.bonus-profic: At 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Religion skill.
At 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Religion skill.
2014_subclasses.divine-soul.favored-by-t: Starting at 1st level, divine power guards your destiny. If you fail a saving throw or miss with an attack roll, you can roll 2d4 and add it to the total, possibly changing the outcome. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Can roll 2d4 and add it to the total, possibly changing the outcome. (action).
2014_subclasses.divine-soul.empowered-he: Starting at 6th level, the divine energy flowing through you can empower healing spells. Whenever you or an ally within 60 feet of you rolls dice to determine the number of hit points a spell restores, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll any number of those dice. You can use this feature only once per turn.
Whenever you or an ally within 60 feet of you rolls dice to determine the number of hit points a spell restores, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll.
2014_subclasses.divine-soul.otherworldly: At 14th level, you can use a bonus action to manifest a pair of spectral wings from your back. While the wings are present, you have a flying speed of 30 feet. The wings last until you are incapacitated, you die, or you dismiss them as a bonus action. You can create the wings a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
As a bonus action, manifest spectral wings. While present, you have a flying speed of 30 feet. The wings last until you are incapacitated or die.
2014_subclasses.divine-soul.unnerving-de: Starting at 18th level, you can channel divine power to protect yourself from harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your sorcerer level + your Charisma modifier. If the damage is reduced to 0, the attacker takes psychic damage equal to half the damage you would have taken.
The attacker takes psychic damage equal to half the damage you would have taken. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.draconic.description: Your innate magic comes from draconic magic that was mingled with your blood or that of your ancestors. Most often, sorcerers with this origin trace their descent back to a mighty sorcerer of ancient times who made a bargain with a dragon or who might even have claimed a dragon parent. Some of these bloodlines are well established in the world, but most are obscure. Any given sorcerer could be the first of a new bloodline, as a result of a pact or some other exceptional circumstance.
2014_subclasses.draconic.dragon-ancestor:
At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.
The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later. (action).
2014_subclasses.draconic.draconic-resili:
As magic flows through your body, it causes physical traits of your dragon ancestors to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
Your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier. (action).
2014_subclasses.draconic.elemental-affin: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.
Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll.
2014_subclasses.draconic.dragon-wings.de:
At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.
2014_subclasses.draconic.dragon-wings.su: At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.draconic.draconic-presen: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.
A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours. (action).
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.description: You are a creature of shadow, for you have drawn on the power of the Shadowfell itself. You can call on the dim power of the plane of shadow to bend light and darkness to your will.
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.eyes-of-the-dar: Starting at 1st level, you have darkvision with a range of 120 feet. When you reach 3rd level in this class, you learn the darkness spell, which doesn't count against your number of spells known. In addition, you can cast that spell by spending 2 sorcery points, and you can see through the darkness created by the spell.
Starting at 1st level, you have darkvision with a range of 120 feet. (action).
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.strength-of-the: Starting at 1st level, the magic of the Shadowfell wards your soul. When damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). On a success, you drop to 1 hit point instead. You can't use this feature if you are reduced to 0 hit points by radiant damage or by a critical hit. After the saving throw succeeds, you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
Can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). (action).
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.hound-of-ill-om:
At 6th level, you gain the ability to call forth a howling creature of darkness to harass your foes. As a bonus action, you can spend 3 sorcery points to summon a hound of ill omen to target one creature you can see within 120 feet of you. The hound uses the dire wolf stat block, with the following changes: The hound is a fiend, not a beast. It appears with a number of temporary hit points equal to half your sorcerer level. It can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object. The hound disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points, if it is more than 30 feet away from you for more than 1 minute, or if you use this feature again.

On each of your turns, you can use your bonus action to command the hound to move to a space within 5 feet of the target and make an attack roll against it. The hound can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
The hound disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points, if it is more than 30 feet away from you for more than 1 minute, or if you use.
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.shadow-walk.des: At 14th level, you gain the ability to step from one shadow into another. When you are in dim light or darkness, as a bonus action, you can teleport up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness.
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.shadow-walk.sum: As a bonus action, you can teleport up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.umbral-form.des: Starting at 18th level, you can use a bonus action to spend 5 sorcery points to transform your body into living shadow for 1 minute. While in this form, you have resistance to all damage except psychic and radiant damage, and you can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. You take 5 force damage if you end your turn inside an object. In addition, you are invisible while you are in dim light or darkness.
2014_subclasses.shadow-2.umbral-form.sum: Take 5 force damage if you end your turn inside an object. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.storm-sorcery.descriptio: Your magic springs from a connection to the elemental power of the storm. Many storm sorcerers can trace their magic to a near-death experience caused by a powerful storm, but perhaps your magic comes from a more distant source.
2014_subclasses.storm-sorcery.wind-speak: The arcane magic you command is infused with elemental air. You can speak, read, and write Primordial. Knowing this language allows you to understand and be understood by those who speak its dialects: Aquan, Auran, Ignan, and Terran.
The arcane magic you command is infused with elemental air. (action).
2014_subclasses.storm-sorcery.tempestuou: Starting at 1st level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to cause whirling gusts of elemental air to briefly surround you, immediately before or after you cast a spell of 1st level or higher. Doing so allows you to fly up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
Doing so allows you to fly up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.storm-sorcery.heart-of-t: At 6th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. In addition, whenever you start casting a spell of 1st level or higher that deals lightning or thunder damage, stormy magic erupts from you. This magic forces each creature of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw. The creature takes lightning or thunder damage (your choice) equal to half your sorcerer level on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
This magic forces each creature of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw.
2014_subclasses.storm-sorcery.storm-guid: At 6th level, you gain the ability to subtly control the weather around you. If it is raining, you can use an action to cause the rain to stop falling in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on you. You can end this effect as a bonus action. If it is windy, you can use a bonus action on your turn to choose the direction that the wind is blowing in a 100-foot-radius sphere centered on you. The wind blows in that direction until the end of your next turn. This feature doesn't alter the speed of the wind.
Doesn't alter the speed of the wind. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.storm-sorcery.storm-s-fu: Starting at 14th level, when you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to the attacker. The damage equals your sorcerer level, and the attacker must also make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker is pushed up to 20 feet away from you.
On a failed save, the attacker is pushed up to 20 feet away from you. (reaction).
At 18th level, you gain immunity to lightning and thunder damage. You also gain a magical flying speed of 60 feet. As an action, you can reduce your flying speed to 30 feet for 1 hour and choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier. The chosen creatures gain a magical flying speed of 30 feet for 1 hour. Once you reduce your flying speed in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
Also gain a magical flying speed of 60 feet. (action).
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.description:
Your innate magic comes from the chaos of wild magic. The raw, uncontrolled magical energy that flows through you can manifest in unpredictable ways, creating random magical effects when you cast spells.

Wild Magic sorcerers are born with chaotic magic that surges within them. This power can be both a blessing and a curse, granting great strength but also carrying the risk of catastrophic magical surges.
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.wild-magic-su: Starting at 1st level, your spellcasting can unleash surges of untamed magic. Immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. If you roll a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Surge table to create a random magical effect. A surge can occur once per turn. If a surge effect is a spell, it is too wild to be affected by your Metamagic. Wild Magic Surge Table (d100): 01-02: Roll on this table at the start of each of your turns for the next minute, ignoring this result on subsequent rolls. 03-04: For the next minute, you can see any invisible creature if you have line of sight to it. 05-06: A modron chosen and controlled by the DM appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later. 07-08: You cast Fireball as a 3rd-level spell centered on yourself. 09-10: You cast Magic Missile as a 5th-level spell. 11-12: Roll a d10. Your height changes by a number of inches equal to the roll. If the roll is odd, you shrink. If the roll is even, you grow. 13-14: You cast Confusion centered on yourself. 15-16: For the next minute, you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns. 17-18: Your head grows to the size of a watermelon for the next minute. 19-20: You cast Fly on a random creature within 60 feet of you. 21-22: You become invisible for the next minute. During that time, other creatures can't hear you. The invisibility ends if you attack or cast a spell. 23-24: A spectral shield hovers near you for the next minute, granting a +2 bonus to AC and immunity to Magic Missile. 25-26: You can't speak for the next minute. Pink bubbles float out of your mouth whenever you try. 27-28: A unicorn controlled by the DM appears in a space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later. 29-30: You cast Fog Cloud centered on yourself. 31-32: Up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you take 4d10 lightning damage. 33-34: You are frightened by the nearest creature until the end of your next turn. 35-36: Each creature within 30 feet of you becomes invisible for the next minute. The invisibility ends on a creature when it attacks or casts a spell. 37-38: You gain resistance to all damage for the next minute. 39-40: Your skin turns a vibrant shade of blue for 1d10 days. 41-42: A creature other than you within 30 feet of you is poisoned for 1d4 hours. 43-44: You cast Polymorph on yourself. If you fail the saving throw, you turn into a sheep for the duration. 45-46: For the next minute, any flammable object you touch that isn't being worn or carried bursts into flame. 47-48: You regain your lowest-level expended spell slot. 49-50: For the next minute, you must shout when you speak. 51-52: You cast Mirror Image on yourself. 53-54: You cast Fly on a random creature within 30 feet of you. 55-56: You become invisible for the next minute. During that time, other creatures can't hear you. The invisibility ends if you attack or cast a spell. 57-58: You cast Stinking Cloud centered on yourself. 59-60: Up to three creatures you choose within 30 feet of you take 4d10 fire damage. 61-62: You cast Speak with Dead. 63-64: You can immediately take one additional action. 65-66: You are teleported up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see. 67-68: The nearest door within 60 feet of you becomes a portal to a random plane for 1 minute. 69-70: A unicorn controlled by the DM appears in a space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later. 71-72: You are teleported to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn, after which time you return to the space you previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space. 73-74: Maximize the damage of the next damaging spell you cast at a higher level. 75-76: Roll a d10. Your age changes by a number of years equal to the roll. If the roll is odd, you get younger (minimum 1 year). If the roll is even, you get older. 77-78: 1d6 flumphs controlled by the DM appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you and are frightened of you. They vanish after 1 minute. 79-80: You cast Polymorph on yourself. If you fail the saving throw, you turn into a sheep for the duration. 81-82: For the next minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action on each of your turns. 83-84: You cast Sunburst centered on yourself. 85-86: A mind flayer chosen and controlled by the DM appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, then disappears 1 minute later. 87-88: For the next minute, a random creature within 60 feet of you is poisoned. 89-90: You are immune to intoxication for the next 5d6 days. 91-92: Your hands become covered in sticky goo for the next minute. 93-94: You cast Greater Invisibility on yourself. 95-96: Your gender is changed for 1d10 days. 97-98: The next creature you hit with an attack takes an extra 1d6 force damage from the attack. 99-00: You regain all expended sorcery points.
97-98: The next creature you hit with an attack takes an extra 1d6 force damage from the attack. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.tides-of-chao: Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate the forces of chance and chaos to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again. Any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher. You then regain the use of this feature.
Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate the forces of chance and chaos to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. (action).
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.bend-luck.des: Starting at 6th level, you have the ability to twist fate using your wild magic. When another creature you can see makes an ability check or a saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll 4d4 and apply the number rolled as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature's ability check or saving throw. You can do so after the creature rolls but before the outcome is determined.
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.bend-luck.sum: You have the ability to twist fate using your wild magic.
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.controlled-ch: At 14th level, you gain a modicum of control over the surges of your wild magic. Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you can roll twice and use either number.
At 14th level, you gain a modicum of control over the surges of your wild magic. (action).
2014_subclasses.wild-magic.spell-bombard: At 18th level, the power of your spells is amplified by the magic of chaos. When you roll damage for a spell and roll the same number on two or more of the dice, you can reroll one of the dice. You must use the new roll, and you can only use this feature once per turn.
When you roll damage for a spell and roll the same number on two or more dice, you can reroll one of those dice. You must use the new roll.
2014_subclasses.archfey.description:
Your patron is a lord or lady of the fey, a creature of legend who holds secrets that were forgotten before the mortal races were born. These beings are capricious and unpredictable, but they can grant great power to those who serve them.

The Archfey patron represents the wild magic of the fey courts. Warlocks who serve these beings gain abilities that reflect the fey's connection to nature and illusion, including the power to charm and beguile others.
2014_subclasses.archfey.fey-presence.des: Starting at 1st level, your patron bestows upon you the ability to project the beguiling and fearsome presence of the fey. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. The creatures that fail their saving throws are all charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
2014_subclasses.archfey.fey-presence.sum: The creatures that fail their saving throws are all charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn. (action).
2014_subclasses.archfey.misty-escape.des: Starting at 6th level, you can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
2014_subclasses.archfey.misty-escape.sum: Can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.archfey.beguiling-defens: Beginning at 10th level, your patron teaches you how to turn the mind-affecting magic of your enemies against them. You are immune to being charmed, and when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.
The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any.
2014_subclasses.archfey.dark-delirium.de: Starting at 14th level, you can plunge a creature into an illusory realm. As an action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a spell). This effect ends early if the creature takes any damage. Until this illusion ends, the creature thinks it is lost in a misty realm, the appearance of which you choose. The creature can see and hear only itself, you, and the illusion. You must finish a short or long rest before you can use this feature again.
2014_subclasses.archfey.dark-delirium.su: Choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. (action).
2014_subclasses.fiend.description: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Fiends powerful enough to forge a pact include demon lords such as Demogorgon, Orcus, Fraz'Urb-luu, and Baphomet; archdevils such as Asmodeus, Dispater, Mephistopheles, and Belial; pit fiends and balors that are especially mighty; and ultroloths and other lords of the yugoloths.
2014_subclasses.fiend.dark-one-s-blessin: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).
When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).
2014_subclasses.fiend.dark-one-s-own-luc:
Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. (action).
2014_subclasses.fiend.fiendish-resilienc: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.
Gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. (action).
Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.
At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
It takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience. (action).
2014_subclasses.great-old-one.descriptio:
Your patron is a being from beyond the stars, an entity of immense power and alien intelligence. The Great Old One might be a sleeping god, an ancient aberration, or a being from another plane of existence entirely.

Those who make pacts with such beings often find their minds expanded, gaining access to telepathic abilities and forbidden knowledge. However, the price of such power can be high, as the Great Old One's influence can slowly drive mortals to madness.
2014_subclasses.great-old-one.awakened-m: At 1st level, you can communicate telepathically.
At 1st level, you can communicate telepathically with any creature within 30 feet of you, provided the creature understands at least one language.
2014_subclasses.great-old-one.entropic-w: At 6th level, you can impose disadvantage on an attack roll against you.
At 6th level, you can impose disadvantage on an attack roll against you. (action).
2014_subclasses.great-old-one.thought-sh: At 10th level, you have resistance to psychic damage.
At 10th level, you have resistance to psychic damage.
2014_subclasses.great-old-one.create-thr: At 14th level, you can charm a creature.

At 14th level, you can charm a creature within 30 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses on a long rest.
2014_subclasses.hexblade.description:
You have made a pact with a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell—a force that manifests in sentient magic weapons. The Hexblade might have forged the blade you wield as your pact weapon, or it might have revealed itself through a ritual of dark binding.

The Hexblade patron represents the power of the Shadowfell and its connection to death and darkness. Warlocks who serve these beings gain abilities that reflect this connection, including the power to curse their enemies and channel dark energy through their weapons.
2014_subclasses.hexblade.hexblade-s-curs: Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to place a bitter curse on someone. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is cursed for 1 minute. The curse ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. Until the curse ends, you gain the following benefits: You gain a bonus to damage rolls against the cursed target. The bonus equals your proficiency bonus. Any attack roll you make against the cursed target is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. If the target dies, you regain hit points equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.hexblade.hex-warrior.des: At 1st level, you acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons. The influence of your patron also allows you to mystically channel your will through a particular weapon. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch one weapon that you are proficient with and that lacks the two-handed property. When you attack with that weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls. This benefit lasts until you finish a long rest again. If you later gain the Pact of the Blade feature, this benefit applies to any pact weapon you conjure with that feature, no matter the weapon's type.
2014_subclasses.hexblade.hex-warrior.sum: Gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons. (action).
2014_subclasses.hexblade.accursed-specte: Starting at 6th level, you can curse the soul of a slain enemy and bind it to your service. When you slay a humanoid, you can cause its spirit to rise as a specter. When the specter appears, it gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level. Roll initiative for the specter, which has its own turns. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you), and it gains a special bonus to its attack rolls equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +0). The specter remains in your service until the end of your next long rest, at which point it vanishes to the afterlife. Once you bind a specter with this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
It gains temporary hit points equal to half your warlock level. (action).
At 10th level, your hex grows more powerful. If the target cursed by your Hexblade's Curse hits you with an attack, roll a d6. On a roll of 4 or higher, the attack instead misses you, regardless of its roll. This ability functions against attack rolls made by both creatures and objects.
This ability functions against attack rolls made by both creatures and objects. (action).
2014_subclasses.hexblade.master-of-hexes: Starting at 14th level, the curse you place on a foe spreads to another when its host falls. When the humanoid you have cursed is reduced to 0 hit points and dies, you can apply the curse to a different humanoid you can see within 30 feet of you. When you transfer the curse, you don't regain uses of the Hexblade's Curse feature.
Can apply the curse to a different humanoid you can see within 30 feet of you. (action).
2014_subclasses.celestial.description: A Celestial patron is a being of the Upper Planes. A celestial warlock is a champion of the forces of good and light, and they channel the power of their patron to heal and protect.
2014_subclasses.celestial.bonus-cantrips: When you choose this patron at 1st level, you learn the sacred flame and light cantrips. They count as warlock cantrips for you, but they don't count against your number of cantrips known.
They count as warlock cantrips for you, but they don't count against your number of cantrips known. (action).
At 1st level, you gain a pool of magical energy represented by a number of d6s equal to 1 + your warlock level. As a bonus action, you can heal one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The maximum number of dice you can spend on a turn equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of one die). Roll the spent dice and add them together. The target regains a number of hit points equal to the total. You regain all expended dice when you finish a long rest.
Can heal one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.celestial.radiant-soul.d: Starting at 6th level, your connection to the Celestial allows you to serve as a conduit for radiant energy. You have resistance to radiant damage. Whenever you cast a spell that deals radiant or fire damage, you add your Charisma modifier to one radiant or fire damage roll of that spell against one of its targets.
2014_subclasses.celestial.radiant-soul.s: Whenever you cast a spell that deals radiant or fire damage, you add your Charisma modifier to one radiant or fire damage roll of that spell against one of its.
2014_subclasses.celestial.celestial-resi: Starting at 10th level, you can draw on the resilience of the Celestial to protect yourself and your allies. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage type until the end of the current turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage type until the end of the current turn. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.celestial.searing-vengea: At 14th level, the radiant energy you channel allows you to overcome death's grasp. When you are reduced to 0 hit points and aren't killed outright, you can use your reaction to instead drop to 1 hit point and shed bright light in a 30-foot radius. Each of your foes within that radius takes 2d8 + your Charisma modifier radiant damage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Each of your foes within that radius takes 2d8 + your Charisma modifier radiant damage. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.fathomless.description: You have made a pact with an entity of the deep sea. A fathomless warlock is a champion of the dark depths, and they channel the power of their patron to control the waters and the creatures that dwell within them.
At 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Fathomless Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.

1st: create or destroy water, thunderwave
3rd: gust of wind, silence
5th: lightning bolt, sleet storm
7th: control water, summon elemental
9th: Bigby's hand, cone of cold
11th: conjure elemental, maelstrom
Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.
2014_subclasses.fathomless.tentacle-of-t: At 1st level, you can summon a spectral tentacle that strikes at your foes. As a bonus action, you can create a 10-foot-long tentacle at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The tentacle lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature to create another tentacle. When you create the tentacle, you can make a melee spell attack against one creature within 10 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. The tentacle can attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. The damage increases to 2d8 at 5th level, 3d8 at 11th level, and 4d8 at 17th level.
On a hit, the target takes 1d8 cold damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.fathomless.gift-of-the-s: At 6th level, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.
At 6th level, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.
At 10th level, you gain resistance to cold damage. In addition, while you are fully submerged in water, you can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed.
At 10th level, gain resistance to cold damage. While fully submerged in water, you can communicate simple ideas with any beast that has an innate swimming speed.
2014_subclasses.fathomless.guardian-coil: At 14th level, your tentacle can defend you and your allies. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to choose one of the creatures and reduce the damage by 1d8. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can make a melee spell attack against the attacker as part of the same reaction. On a hit, the attacker takes 1d8 + your Charisma modifier cold damage.
Can use your reaction to choose one of the creatures and reduce the damage by 1d8. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.fathomless.grasping-tent: At 18th level, you can call forth a manifestation of the deep. You can cast the evard's black tentacles spell, requiring no spell slot or material components. When you cast the spell in this way, the area of the spell is difficult terrain for creatures other than you. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest. (action).
2014_subclasses.genie.description: You have made a pact with one of the genies, the mighty elemental rulers of the Inner Planes. A genie patron is a powerful being that can grant wishes and bend reality to its will.
2014_subclasses.genie.bonus-spells.descr:
At 1st level, you learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Genie Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.

1st: detect evil and good, protection from evil and good
3rd: create food and water, phantasmal killer
5th: creation, sending
7th: creation, summon elemental
9th: creation, wall of stone
11th: creation, wish
2014_subclasses.genie.bonus-spells.summa: Each of these spells counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn't count against your number of warlock spells you know.
2014_subclasses.genie.genie-s-vessel.des:
At 1st level, your patron gifts you a magical vessel that grants you a measure of the genie's power. The vessel is a Tiny object, and you choose the object's nature: an oil lamp, an ornate urn, a gilded chalice, or some other similarly shaped Tiny object. While you are touching the vessel, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells. The vessel's AC equals your spell save DC. It has a number of hit points equal to your warlock level + your proficiency bonus, and it is immune to poison and psychic damage.

The vessel grants you the following benefits:

Elemental Gift: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.

Limited Wish: Once per long rest, you can cast a spell of 6th level or lower from the warlock spell list, requiring no spell slot or material components.
2014_subclasses.genie.genie-s-vessel.sum: The vessel grants you the following benefits: Elemental Gift: You gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor. (action).
2014_subclasses.genie.elemental-gift.des: Starting at 6th level, the vessel grants you resistance to a damage type based on your patron's kind: fire (Dao), cold (Djinni), lightning (Efreeti), or thunder (Marid). You also gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.
2014_subclasses.genie.elemental-gift.sum: Also gain a flying speed of 30 feet, which works only while you are not wearing heavy armor.
2014_subclasses.genie.sanctuary-vessel.d: At 10th level, when you or an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to whisk the damaged creature into your vessel. The creature is transported to the vessel's extradimensional space, where it is safe from harm. The creature remains there until the end of your next turn or until you use this feature again. When the creature reappears, it appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
2014_subclasses.genie.sanctuary-vessel.s: At 10th level, when you or an ally within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to whisk the damaged creature into your vessel. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.genie.limited-wish.descr: At 14th level, you can tap into the power of your genie patron to cast powerful spells. Once per long rest, you can cast a spell of 6th level or lower from the warlock spell list, requiring no spell slot or material components.
2014_subclasses.genie.limited-wish.summa: At 14th level, you can tap into the power of your genie patron to cast powerful spells.
2014_subclasses.the-undead.description: You've made a pact with a powerful undead being, such as a vampire, lich, or mummy lord. This patron grants you power over death and undeath, allowing you to channel the chill of the grave and command the spirits of the dead.
2014_subclasses.the-undead.form-of-dread: You can use a bonus action to transform into a terrifying visage of death. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn. You can transform a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Gain the following benefits: You gain temporary hit points equal to 1d10 + your warlock level. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.the-undead.grave-touched: Your patron's power changes your body. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can change the damage type of the attack to necrotic damage. While you are in your Form of Dread, you can also change the damage type of any spell you cast to necrotic damage.
In addition, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, you can change the damage type of the attack to necrotic damage.
2014_subclasses.the-undead.necrotic-husk: Your body is suffused with necrotic energy. You have resistance to necrotic damage. In addition, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you takes necrotic damage equal to your warlock level + your Charisma modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
In addition, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead, and each creature of your choice within 30.
2014_subclasses.the-undead.spirit-projec: As an action, you can project your spirit from your body. Your body is unconscious and appears dead while your spirit is projected. Your spirit resembles a spectral version of your body and has the following statistics: It has 1 hit point and immunity to all damage except force damage. It can't take actions or cast spells. It can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. While projected, you can use your action to return to your body. Your body regains consciousness when your spirit returns to it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
It has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover. (action).
2014_subclasses.undying.description:
Your patron is a powerful undead being, such as a lich, vampire, or mummy lord. These beings have cheated death and gained immortality through dark magic, and they share some of their power with their warlock servants.

The Undying patron represents those who have transcended death, and its warlocks gain abilities that reflect this connection to undeath. They can resist disease, recover from wounds, and even cheat death itself.
2014_subclasses.undying.among-the-dead.d: At 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
2014_subclasses.undying.among-the-dead.s: At 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
2014_subclasses.undying.undying-nature.d: Also at 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against disease.
2014_subclasses.undying.undying-nature.s: Also at 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against disease.
2014_subclasses.undying.beyond-the-grave: At 6th level, you can gain temporary hit points when you finish a short rest.
At 6th level, you can gain temporary hit points when you finish a short rest.
2014_subclasses.undying.indestructible-l: At 10th level, you can regain hit points when you take damage.
At 10th level, you can regain hit points when you take damage.
2014_subclasses.undying.undying-nature-2: At 14th level, you can't be killed by a single attack.
At 14th level, you can't be killed by a single attack.
2014_subclasses.abjuration.description:
The abjuration specialist is a wizard who focuses on protective and defensive magic. They are masters of wards, shields, and counterspells, able to protect themselves and their allies from magical and physical harm.

Abjurers study the theory and practice of defensive magic, learning to create magical barriers that can absorb damage and deflect attacks. They are often found on the front lines, using their abilities to keep their companions safe.
2014_subclasses.abjuration.abjuration-sa: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.
At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
2014_subclasses.abjuration.arcane-ward.d: Also at 2nd level, you can create a magical ward.
2014_subclasses.abjuration.arcane-ward.s: At 2nd level, when you cast an abjuration spell, you create a magical ward with Hit Points equal to twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. The ward takes damage first and recharges when you cast an abjuration spell.
2014_subclasses.abjuration.projected-war: At 6th level, you can use your Arcane Ward to protect others.
At 6th level, you can use your Arcane Ward to protect others. (action).
2014_subclasses.abjuration.improved-abju: At 10th level, your Arcane Ward regains hit points when you finish a short rest.
At 10th level, your Arcane Ward regains hit points when you finish a short rest.
2014_subclasses.abjuration.spell-resista: At 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells.
At 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells.
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.description: Bladesingers are elves who have learned to combine swordplay with arcane magic. They are deadly warriors who use their magic to enhance their combat prowess.
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.bonus-profi: When you choose this tradition at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with light armor, a one-handed melee weapon of your choice, and the Performance skill if you don't already have it.
Gain proficiency with light armor, a one-handed melee weapon of your choice, and the Performance skill if you don't already have it. (action).
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.training-in: Starting at 2nd level, you learn to blend your magic with your weapon work. You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: Acrobatics, Athletics, History, or Performance. You also gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.
Also gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.bladesong.d:
Starting at 2nd level, you can invoke a secret elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield. It graces you with supernatural speed, agility, and focus. You can use a bonus action to start the Bladesong, which lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are incapacitated, if you don medium or heavy armor or a shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. You can also dismiss the Bladesong at any time you choose (no action required). While your Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits:

You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

You have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.

You gain a bonus to any Constitution saving throw you make to maintain your concentration on a spell. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.bladesong.s: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. (bonus action).
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.extra-attac: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.
Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. (only when taking the attack action, permanent, scales).
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.song-of-def: At 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your Bladesong is active. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to expend one spell slot and reduce that damage to you by an amount equal to five times the spell slot's level.
At 10th level, you can direct your magic to absorb damage while your Bladesong is active. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.bladesinging.song-of-vic: At 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.
At 14th level, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Bladesong is active.
2014_subclasses.chronurgy.description: Chronurgy is the study of time magic. Chronurgists learn to manipulate the flow of time, slowing it down, speeding it up, or even reversing it.
Starting at 2nd level, you can magically exert limited control over the flow of time around a creature. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll a d8 and apply it to the roll. You can choose to use this feature after the roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack roll, ability check, or saving throw succeeds or fails. The d8 roll is added to the total if the roll is for an attack roll or ability check, or subtracted from the total if the roll is for a saving throw. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
An ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to roll a d8 and apply it to the roll. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.chronurgy.temporal-aware: Starting at 2nd level, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier. In addition, you can't be surprised while you are conscious.
Starting at 2nd level, you gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier. (action).
2014_subclasses.chronurgy.momentary-stas: Starting at 6th level, you can use your command over time to force a creature to slow down. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is restrained and incapacitated until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Can choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. (action).
2014_subclasses.chronurgy.arcane-abeyanc: At 10th level, you can store a spell in a tiny, bead-like object. As an action, you can cast a spell of 4th level or lower into the bead, which holds the spell until it is used. The bead is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. The bead is destroyed when the spell is cast or when you die. You can have only one bead at a time, and you can't create another until the spell in the bead is cast. The bead can be used by anyone who holds it. To use the spell, the creature holding the bead must use its action to cast the spell, using your spell save DC and spell attack bonus.
The bead is a Tiny object, and it has AC 10, 1 hit point, and immunity to all damage except force damage. (action).
2014_subclasses.chronurgy.convergent-fut: Starting at 14th level, you can peer into the future and see the outcome of a course of action. When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to ignore the roll. Instead, you can choose the result of the roll to be the highest or lowest possible. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
An ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to ignore the roll. (reaction).
2014_subclasses.conjuration.description:
Conjurers specialize in creating objects and creatures from nothing. They can summon weapons, armor, and even living creatures to aid them in battle or perform tasks.

The study of conjuration requires precision and spatial awareness. Conjurers learn to open portals to other planes, calling forth creatures and objects to serve their needs. They are versatile spellcasters who can adapt to any situation.
2014_subclasses.conjuration.conjuration-: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.
At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
2014_subclasses.conjuration.minor-conjur: Also at 2nd level, you can conjure small objects.

At 2nd level, you can conjure a nonmagical object in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. The object can be no larger than 3 feet on a side and weighs no more than 10 pounds. It disappears after 1 hour or if it takes any damage.
2014_subclasses.conjuration.benign-trans: At 6th level, you can swap places with a creature.
At 6th level, as a bonus action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If you teleport within 5 feet of a willing creature, you can swap places with that creature.
2014_subclasses.conjuration.focused-conj: At 10th level, your concentration on conjuration spells is not broken when you take damage.
At 10th level, your concentration on conjuration spells is not broken when you take damage.
2014_subclasses.conjuration.durable-summ: At 14th level, your summoned creatures gain temporary hit points.
At 14th level, your summoned creatures gain temporary hit points.
2014_subclasses.divination.description:
Diviners study the art of predicting the future. They can glimpse moments yet to come, gaining insight into the outcomes of actions and the intentions of others.

The study of divination requires keen intellect and intuition. Diviners learn to read the signs and portents that others miss, using their knowledge to guide their allies and outmaneuver their enemies.
2014_subclasses.divination.divination-sa: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved.
At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
2014_subclasses.divination.portent.descr: Also at 2nd level, you can replace any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.
2014_subclasses.divination.portent.summa: Also at 2nd level, you can replace any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. (action).
2014_subclasses.divination.expert-divina: At 6th level, you can regain spell slots when you cast divination spells.
At 6th level, you can regain spell slots when you cast divination spells.
2014_subclasses.divination.third-eye.des: At 10th level, you can gain darkvision, see invisible creatures, etc.
2014_subclasses.divination.third-eye.sum: At 10th level, you can gain darkvision, see invisible creatures, etc.
2014_subclasses.divination.greater-porte: At 14th level, you can cast the foresight spell once per long rest.
At 14th level, you can cast the foresight spell once per long rest.
2014_subclasses.enchantment.description:
Enchanters specialize in manipulating the minds of others. They can charm, beguile, and control creatures, turning enemies into allies and bending others to their will.

The study of enchantment requires subtlety and finesse. Enchanters learn to weave spells that influence thoughts and emotions, using their abilities to avoid conflict or gain advantage in social situations.
2014_subclasses.enchantment.savant.descr: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved.
2014_subclasses.enchantment.savant.summa: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
2014_subclasses.enchantment.hypnotic-gaz: Also at 2nd level, you can charm a creature with a look.
Also at 2nd level, you can charm a creature with a look.
2014_subclasses.enchantment.instinctive-: At 6th level, you can divert attacks made against you.
At 6th level, you can divert attacks made against you.
2014_subclasses.enchantment.split-enchan: At 10th level, you can target two creatures with enchantment spells.
At 10th level, you can target two creatures with enchantment spells.
2014_subclasses.enchantment.alter-memori: At 14th level, you can modify a creature's memory.
At 14th level, when you charm a creature, you can modify its memory of the event. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have its memory altered.
2014_subclasses.evocation.description: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.
2014_subclasses.evocation.evocation-sava: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.
Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved. (action).
Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save. (action).
2014_subclasses.evocation.potent-cantrip: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
The creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.
2014_subclasses.evocation.empowered-evoc: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.
Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast. (action).
2014_subclasses.evocation.overchannel.de:
Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.
2014_subclasses.evocation.overchannel.su: Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. (action).
2014_subclasses.graviturgy.description: Graviturgy is the study of gravity magic. Graviturgists learn to manipulate the force of gravity, making themselves and their allies lighter or heavier, and even creating gravitational anomalies.
2014_subclasses.graviturgy.adjust-densit: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your command of gravity to alter the weight of a creature. As an action, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's weight is halved or doubled (your choice) for 1 minute. While the creature's weight is halved, its walking speed increases by 10 feet, and it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. While the creature's weight is doubled, its walking speed decreases by 10 feet, and it has disadvantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Its walking speed increases by 10 feet, and it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. (action).
Starting at 6th level, you can create a point of intense gravitational force. When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can choose one creature that fails its saving throw. That creature is pulled 10 feet toward you, provided you can see it and it is within 60 feet of you.
That creature is pulled 10 feet toward you, provided you can see it and it is within 60 feet of you. (action).
